name: The Doctor's Office
vibeCheck: A vintage doctor's-office-themed craft cocktail bar on Anna Maria Island — apothecary bottles, eye charts, and a daily 5pm absinthe ritual poured tableside. Intimate and theatrical, an early-evening treat, not a late-night club.
whyGo: One of the area's most distinctive cocktail spots — a physician's-office-themed bar from Beach Bistro's Sean Murphy, where the signature move is the 5pm "Absinthe Hour" and drinks arrive with real ceremony. A destination for a serious, atmospheric cocktail.
bestFor: Cocktail enthusiasts and anyone wanting a theatrical, grown-up drink to start the evening. Not for a late night — it closes by 10–11pm — and the bar room is 21+.
knownFor: Craft cocktails in a mid-century doctor's-office setting — including a daily absinthe service poured tableside — from the team behind Beach Bistro.
powerhouseProof: Created by Sean Murphy, the longtime owner of Anna Maria Island's acclaimed Beach Bistro, and open since 2017.
foodMove: The kitchen sends out chef-driven shareable plates — Gulf seafood and prime tenderloin, served on metal laboratory trays. (Food and wine menus below; cocktails are by reservation, not posted online.)
drinkMove: Come at 5pm for the "Absinthe Hour" — absinthe served with an atomizer and the full louche ritual, the bar's enduring signature. The cocktail list rotates and isn't posted online, so let the bartender steer.
insiderMove: This isn't a hidden-entrance speakeasy — reservations are suggested, so book on Resy or call between 2 and 10pm. Under-21 guests are welcome in the outdoor Doctor's Garden, just not the 21+ bar room.
verifiedStory: The bar is themed as the island's mid-century physician's office — the space reportedly once housed Anna Maria Island's only doctor — and opened in mid-2017, eye charts and all.
funFact: The theme runs deep: absinthe comes via syringe and atomizer, and the daily "medication" punch is served in little medicine cups.
currentUsefulDetail: Open Sun–Thu 5–10pm and Fri–Sat 5–11pm; it's on Holmes Beach (Anna Maria Island), about 40 minutes from downtown Sarasota. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It closes early (10–11pm), so it's a start-the-evening spot, not a late-night bar; the bar room is 21+; and it's a small, popular island room, so reservations are the smart play.

name: The Gator Club
hours: Open nightly, generally to 2am (live music + weekend DJs)
vibeCheck: Downtown Sarasota's historic live-music bar — a century-old brick room on Main Street with bands most nights, a DJ upstairs on weekends, and one of the deepest liquor shelves in town. Loud, lively, open till 2am.
whyGo: The Gator Club is a downtown spirits bar that pours a house Old Fashioned on Buffalo Trace and 1-ounce tastes of its highest-tier bottles, including a house Buffalo Trace TGC barrel-select. The official cocktail board also lists a Sazerac rye Manhattan and a Wheatley vodka espresso martini.
bestFor: Late nights out, live-music fans, and whiskey drinkers who want options. Not for a quiet drink or an early evening — it gets loud and clubby on weekend nights.
knownFor: The Gator Club pours a Buffalo Trace Old Fashioned and rare 1-oz pours.
powerhouseProof: thegatorclub.com whiskey list prints Buffalo Trace TGC Barrel Select Bourbon. thegatorclub.com signature cocktail menu (official image) prints a Buffalo Trace Old Fashioned, Sazerac rye Manhattan, and Wheatley espresso martini. Homepage states 1-oz pours of the highest-tier spirits. NPS NRIS 98000651 lists Worth’s Block / Gator Club.
foodMove: This is a drinks-first bar — food is limited to small eats (pickles, cheese and crackers, chips), so eat before you come.
drinkMove: Skip the cocktail list and work the spirits wall — with 500-plus bottles, this is a bourbon-and-whiskey lover's room; ask the bartender for something you can't get elsewhere.
insiderMove: Ask for a 1-oz pour of the house Buffalo Trace TGC barrel-select, then the Old Fashioned or the Sazerac rye Manhattan. Bottle count, band nights, karaoke, and the upstairs DJ stay in the room notes. Small eats are pickles, cheese and crackers, and chips — not a kitchen plate.
verifiedStory: The pour is the product. The room is Worth’s Block (NPS: built 1912, NRHP 1998, other name Gator Club). Operator copy says “since 1913,” 500-plus bottles, live bands five nights, karaoke, and a second-floor weekend DJ — history and nightlife, not the rail hook.
funFact: Over a century the building has been a saloon, cigar store, grocery, and newsstand — with local lore of bootlegging, gambling, and a resident ghost or two.
currentUsefulDetail: Open late every night, generally until 2am, with live music and DJ nights through the week. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a loud, crowded weekend club scene upstairs — not a spot for a quiet drink — and some live-music or DJ nights may carry a cover charge. Come for the music and the room, not for polish.

name: The O Bar
vibeCheck: A neighborhood sports-and-live-music bar in Osprey — 20-plus TVs, pool, darts, shuffleboard, a covered patio, and BBQ off the kitchen. Casual, local, open till 2am. (Not the rooftop bar the name might suggest.)
whyGo: The O Bar kitchen still lists American bar plates — a sampler basket, cheesy bread, onion rings, and corn-dog nuggets on the official About copy, plus a chicken fajita quesadilla, chicken cordon bleu bites, and beer-battered cod on the posted menu boards.
bestFor: Sports fans, live-music nights, and locals who want a casual late drink and some barbecue. Not for a cocktail-forward or upscale evening.
knownFor: The O Bar plates chicken fajita quesadillas, cordon bleu bites, and beer-battered cod
powerhouseProof: About HTML still names the sampler basket, cheesy bread, onion rings, and corn-dog nuggets. Official menu images still list the chicken fajita quesadilla, chicken cordon bleu bites, and beer-battered cod.
foodMove: Barbecue is the food angle here — there's a dedicated BBQ menu alongside the bar fare ($–$$). (Menu link below.)
insiderMove: TV packages, shuffleboard, pool, patio, and the separate smoking area belong here, not in knownFor/whyGo. Kitchen-late and the dated Monday BBQ board are schedule/deal copy, not the hook. Address stays off the rails.
verifiedStory: Official About copy still sells a late American kitchen beside the sports room — more than twenty TVs, a 22-foot shuffleboard, three billiard tables, two dart boards, a covered patio with TVs, and a separate smoking yard. Those amenities stay in the story file. The rails sell the plates.
funFact: Despite the name, it's not a rooftop or hotel "O bar" — it's a down-to-earth Osprey sports bar that also books live bands.
currentUsefulDetail: Generally open daily 11am–2am, with live music on select nights. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a casual Osprey sports bar, not the rooftop cocktail spot the name might imply, and its online menu is image-only — check current offerings on site.

name: Venice Train Depot
hours: Free Saturday docent tours ~10am–1pm (check VAHS calendar)
vibeCheck: A beautifully restored 1927 railroad depot in downtown Venice — now a free local-history museum with a circus twist, complete with a vintage Pullman circus car and a caboose parked outside. Small, characterful, and genuinely historic.
whyGo: A free glimpse of Venice's railroad-and-circus past — the restored 1927 Seaboard Air Line depot houses the Venice Area Historical Society's museum, with railcar exhibits and a 1953 Pullman circus car in the adjacent park. A quick, kid-friendly history stop.
bestFor: History buffs, families, and train or circus fans wanting a short, free downtown stop. Not a big attraction — it's a compact museum with limited public hours.
knownFor: Being the restored 1927 Venice Train Depot — a former Seaboard Air Line passenger station, now a local-history and circus museum on the National Register of Historic Places.
powerhouseProof: A Mediterranean Revival depot opened on March 27, 1927, listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1989 and restored in 2002–2003.
insiderMove: Free docent-led tours run on Saturdays (roughly 10am–1pm), so time your visit for the weekend; admission is free (donations welcome), and the railroad park with the circus car and caboose is open to wander.
verifiedStory: The depot opened in 1927 as a Seaboard Air Line Railway station; after falling out of rail use, it was restored in 2002–2003 and now houses the Venice Area Historical Society's museum in its two former waiting-room halls.
funFact: Out back in Rollins W. Coakley Railroad Park sit a restored 1953 Pullman circus car and a 1974 caboose — a nod to Venice's decades as a circus winter town.
currentUsefulDetail: Admission is free (donations appreciated); free docent tours run Saturdays, roughly 10am–1pm — check the Venice Area Historical Society calendar for exact dates. The depot is also rentable for private events. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a small museum with limited public hours (mainly Saturday tours), not a full-day attraction — check the schedule before going, since parts are often booked for private events.

name: Epiphany Cathedral
hours: Office Mon–Fri 8am–4pm; Sunday Mass 7:30, 9, 11am & 5:30pm (Sat vigils 3, 4:30, 6pm; weekdays 8:30am)
vibeCheck: The seat of a ten-county diocese carries the hushed gravity of a mother church — reverent, active, and unmistakably a working parish rather than a sightseeing stop. At the moment that gravity comes with hard hats: the cathedral is mid-rebuild.
whyGo: It's the cathedral of the Diocese of Venice — the region's principal Catholic church — so you come for Mass, a quiet moment, or the diocesan weight of the place. Just know the visitable landmark is on pause: the building won't reopen until the reconstruction wraps, targeted around 2027.
bestFor: Catholics attending Mass in Venice, or church-architecture fans willing to circle back in 2027 for the new barrel-vault nave, mosaic altarpiece and bell tower.
knownFor: Being the cathedral — the mother church and bishop's seat of the Diocese of Venice in Florida, which spans ten counties from Sarasota south toward the Everglades.
powerhouseProof: Mother church of a ten-county diocese created by Pope John Paul II in 1984; the current reconstruction adds roughly 300 seats, hurricane-rated stained glass and a new bell tower.
insiderMove: During construction, on-site parking shrinks — overflow is the bus lot on Harbor Boulevard — and Mass is held in the Parish Center, not the church, so confirm the location before you go.
verifiedStory: It began in 1935 as a mission of Sarasota's St. Martha's parish; the present church was dedicated on June 29, 1980, and became a cathedral in 1984 when Pope John Paul II created the Diocese of Venice.
funFact: The parish's first church was military surplus — in 1947 a former chapel from the Venice Army Air Base was physically hauled to Tampa Avenue, refurbished, and re-dedicated as the first Epiphany Church.
currentUsefulDetail: The cathedral is in a roughly two-year reconstruction (demolition began June 2024); until it reopens — targeted around 2027 — all Masses are held in the Parish Center and the Memorial Garden is closed. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: This is an active place of worship, not a tourist stop — come for Mass or quiet reflection, dress modestly, and mind service times. And there's little to see right now: the church itself is a closed construction site with worship moved to the Parish Center.

name: Alvin's Island
hours: Call to confirm (beach-store hours; not posted online)
vibeCheck: A tropical beach superstore on Anna Maria Island — swimsuits, souvenirs, beach toys, and resortwear under one roof, steps from the sand. Touristy and cheap-and-cheerful, the classic "we forgot the sunscreen" stop.
whyGo: The one-stop beach shop on Anna Maria Island — swimwear, towels, toys, and souvenirs when you've forgotten something or want a cheap beach kit. Budget-friendly and right by the sand.
bestFor: Tourists and beachgoers who need beach gear or a souvenir. Not for anyone after quality or a boutique find — it's budget tourist goods.
knownFor: Being a tropical beach superstore — swimwear, beachwear, souvenirs, and beach toys — part of the Southeast's largest beach-store chain.
powerhouseProof: Part of Alvin's Island, a beach-store chain founded in Panama City Beach in 1957 and grown to 34 stores across Florida and Alabama — the largest beach-store chain in the Southeast.
insiderMove: It's a walkable stop near the Holmes Beach sand for anything you forgot; watch for buy-one-get-one deals, and set expectations — this is buy-for-the-trip gear, not buy-for-the-decade.
verifiedStory: The chain started as a single store on Front Beach Road in Panama City Beach in 1957 and has grown to 34 locations across Florida and Alabama.
funFact: What looks like a small local beach shop is actually part of the Southeast's largest beach-store chain — 34 stores dating back to 1957.
currentUsefulDetail: This is the Holmes Beach store (#753) on Anna Maria Island; posted hours weren't confirmable online, so call ahead, though beach stores like this typically keep long daily hours. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's touristy and budget-quality — reviews are mixed-to-low, with some noting items that don't last. Buy for the trip, not for keeps, and call ahead since hours aren't posted online.

name: Barnes & Noble
vibeCheck: A full-size Barnes & Noble on the South Trail with a café in back — the reliable rainy-afternoon, kill-an-hour, buy-a-gift bookstore, not a destination.
whyGo: When you need an actual bookstore — a specific title, a kids' gift, a café seat, or a Saturday story time — this South Trail location covers it, across from Trader Joe's.
bestFor: A rainy afternoon, a last-minute gift, or a Saturday morning with little kids (there's a weekly story time).
knownFor: A full-service bookstore with a Café, plus toys, games, media and gifts — the one-stop book-and-gift run on the South Trail.
foodMove: There's an in-store Café for coffee and a snack — handy if you're settling in with a stack.
insiderMove: It's across from Trader Joe's in the Glengary Shoppes, so pair the two errands; bring the kids for the weekly Saturday 11am Storytime.
currentUsefulDetail: A recurring in-store Storytime runs Saturdays at 11am. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a chain bookstore in a strip plaza — set expectations accordingly. And note there are two Barnes & Nobles in Sarasota: this is the South Trail store (4010 S Tamiami), not the newer University Town Center location about eight miles north.

name: Cocoplum village shops
hours: Open-air center; hours vary by store
vibeCheck: An open-air, Publix-anchored shopping center in North Port — national chains for groceries, home goods, beauty, and sporting goods under one roof. A practical errands hub, not a boutique district.
whyGo: A one-stop errands run in North Port — Publix plus Dick's Sporting Goods, TJ Maxx, Ross, Hobby Lobby, Ulta, and Bealls in one open-air center. Handy if you're in the south end of the county and need to knock out shopping.
bestFor: Practical errands and national-brand shopping under one roof. Not a destination or a boutique browse — it's a chain-anchored power center.
knownFor: Being North Port's Publix-anchored open-air shopping center — groceries plus national retailers like Dick's, TJ Maxx, Ross, Hobby Lobby, and Ulta.
insiderMove: It's a big open-air center with free surface parking, so it's an easy errands stop; occasional Cars & Coffee car shows gather near the Hobby Lobby end.
currentUsefulDetail: An open-air, Publix-anchored center in North Port (at the south end of Sarasota County, about 35 minutes from Sarasota); hours vary by store. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a national-chain power center, not the boutique waterfront vibe of the Lakewood Ranch districts, so set expectations. And it's in North Port, a fair drive from central Sarasota.

name: Detwiler's Farm Market
vibeCheck: A big, no-frills family farm market on Lockwood Ridge — piled-high local and Amish produce, a real butcher and seafood counter, deli, and bakery, all at farm-stand prices. A genuine grocery run, not a boutique.
whyGo: The local pick for cheap, fresh produce and a proper butcher and fish counter — a family-run farm market (one of six) that's been a Sarasota staple since 2002. Worth the trip if you're stocking up or after Gulf seafood and Amish goods.
bestFor: Locals and visitors doing a real grocery run who want farm-stand prices and local produce. Not a quick convenience stop or a gift-shop browse.
knownFor: Fresh local and Amish produce, a full butcher and seafood market, an old-fashioned deli, and an in-store bakery — a value-priced family farm market.
powerhouseProof: A family-owned Sarasota farm market since 2002 — grown from a 10-by-20-foot tent to six stores, run by Henry Detwiler Sr., his wife, and their nine children.
insiderMove: This University/Lockwood Ridge branch is open until 8pm (later than the Palmer store) — but it's closed Sundays, so plan a Monday-through-Saturday run.
verifiedStory: Founder Henry Detwiler Sr., raised Mennonite in Pennsylvania, moved to Sarasota in 1986 and started with a roughly 10-by-20-foot tent at an egg farm; the "Detwiler's Farm Market" name began with the Palmer Boulevard store in 2008.
funFact: It's closed every Sunday by design — the faith-driven family shuts the doors, so plan your grocery run for the rest of the week.
currentUsefulDetail: This is the Lockwood Ridge (University) location, open Monday–Saturday 8am–8pm and closed Sundays; it's one of six Detwiler's stores. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: Closed Sundays, and it's a busy working grocery — parking and checkout get tight at peak times. There are six branches, so make sure you're headed to this Lockwood Ridge one.

name: Green Turtle Shell & Gift Shop
hours: Call to confirm (hours not reliably posted online)
vibeCheck: A family-owned beach gift shop on Anna Maria Island — shells, sea-turtle souvenirs, local art, jewelry, and beach apparel. A classic browse-and-buy stop for a keepsake or a beach tee.
whyGo: The spot on Anna Maria Island for beach-y gifts and souvenirs — shells, sea-turtle figurines, handcrafted jewelry, local art, and plenty of beach apparel. A quick, fun browse near the sand.
bestFor: Souvenir and gift shoppers browsing Anna Maria Island. Not a destination in itself — a pleasant add-on stop.
knownFor: Being a family-owned beach gift shop on Anna Maria Island — shells, sea-turtle souvenirs, beach apparel, local art, and handcrafted jewelry.
insiderMove: It's an easy browse for a souvenir or a beach tee while you're on the island; call ahead if you're making a special trip, since posted hours aren't reliable online.
currentUsefulDetail: A family-owned beach gift shop on Anna Maria Island (Bradenton Beach); posted hours weren't confirmable online, so call ahead. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a small souvenir shop, not a destination, and its hours aren't reliably posted online — call before a special trip. Don't confuse it with the "Gift City" sibling on Siesta Key.

name: Ideal Classic Cars
vibeCheck: A classic-car dealership in Venice with a free, walk-through showroom — rows of restored muscle cars, hot rods, and a few movie and TV cars, all for sale. A no-cost car-lover's browse, not a polished museum.
whyGo: Wander a 27,000-square-foot showroom of classic cars for free — decades of muscle cars, hot rods, and European classics, plus crowd-pleaser movie and TV cars. A fun, no-pressure stop for car fans or a rainy day.
bestFor: Car enthusiasts, families, and anyone wanting a free, low-key browse. Not for someone expecting a formal museum — it's a working dealership and the cars are for sale.
knownFor: Being a classic-car dealership with a free, open-to-the-public showroom — a big rotating inventory of collector cars, trucks, and motorcycles, plus movie-car displays.
powerhouseProof: A full-service classic-car dealership that's sold over 3,700 classics, with a 27,000-square-foot showroom open free to the public.
insiderMove: Admission is free and browsers are welcome — no sales pressure — but it's a working dealership, so the inventory rotates and it's different every visit. Closed Sundays.
funFact: The free showroom is known for its movie and TV cars — visitors often mention spotting crowd-pleasers like a Batmobile, Herbie the Love Bug, and the Scooby-Doo Mystery Machine.
currentUsefulDetail: Open Monday–Thursday 9am–6pm, Friday to 5pm, Saturday to 4pm, and closed Sundays; the showroom is free to walk through. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a working dealership, not a proper museum, so inventory changes and everything's for sale. Some buyer reviews allege misrepresented vehicle condition — a caveat if you're purchasing, less so for a free browse. Closed Sundays.

name: Main Street at Lakewood Ranch
hours: Open-air district; hours vary by shop (Music on Main 1st Fri 6–9pm)
vibeCheck: The original Lakewood Ranch town center — a walkable Main Street of boutiques, cafés, international restaurants, and a six-screen cinema, along a lakeside path. More established and strollable than the newer Waterside.
whyGo: Main Street at Lakewood Ranch marked 20 years in 2025. It is the master-planned town center with a six-screen cinema and a walk along Lake Uihlein — not Waterside Place. Music on Main, first Friday 6–9 p.m., draws about 4,500 people.
bestFor: Evening strolls, dinner-and-a-movie, and monthly community events. Not a historic downtown — it's a master-planned, manicured town center.
knownFor: 2005 LWR town center: cinema, Lake Uihlein, first-Friday Music on Main
powerhouseProof: Observer: ~4,500 people at Music on Main (LWR events manager). Official directory lists Lakewood Ranch Cinemas on this street. Car show: first Wednesday 5–8 p.m. in season (Observer).
insiderMove: First Friday, bring a chair before 6 p.m. — Observer regulars say a late arrival means circling the lot. Sunday farmers-market hours in the operator deals sit at Waterside Place, not on this Main Street page.
verifiedStory: Observer’s 2025 milestone piece treats Main Street as Lakewood Ranch’s stand-in downtown — shops, a six-screen cinema, Lake Uihlein path — on its 20th anniversary. Music on Main began a year after the street opened and is now a first-Friday 6–9 p.m. block party. The operator’s Waterside Place page is a different district.
funFact: Music on Main, the monthly first-Friday street party, now draws around 4,500 people a night.
currentUsefulDetail: An open-air district, so hours vary by shop and restaurant; signature events are Music on Main (first Friday, 6–9pm) and the classic car show (first Wednesday, 5–8pm, in season). Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a manicured, master-planned town center rather than a historic downtown, and the tenant mix has turned over across 20 years. The famous Sunday farmers market is now at Waterside Place, not here.

name: Nokomis Beach Bait & Tackle
vibeCheck: A no-nonsense bait-and-tackle shop a couple of blocks from Nokomis Beach — rods, reels, live and frozen bait, and local intel on where they're biting. Anglers' basics, plus a beach-goods shop next door.
whyGo: Nokomis Beach Bait & Tackle is a working tackle shop: live and frozen bait, plus named rods and reels — Okuma, Redbone, Penn, Falcon, and Ricky Reds — and lure lines Yo-Zuri, Rapala, and DOA. Staff set you up for the jetty and pier; Tormenter and HUK shirts hang next to the counter.
bestFor: Anglers heading to the jetty or beach who need bait, tackle, or local advice. Not a general shopping stop — it's a working bait shop.
knownFor: Nokomis Beach Bait & Tackle stocks live bait plus Okuma, Penn, and Ricky Reds.
powerhouseProof: Homepage and about print live and frozen bait plus named brands (Okuma, Penn, Ricky Reds, Yo-Zuri, Rapala, DOA, Falcon, Redbone). Contact prints 820 Albee Rd W and the 6 a.m. clock. Beach-info post dates the sister beach shop to 2013. Visit Sarasota independently names this shop as the pier/jetty gear stop.
insiderMove: It really does open at 6 a.m. — Sunday only to 5. Call (941) 882-4387 to hold live bait. Walk through to the 2013 Casey Key Beach Shop if the rest of the car wants chairs or a coin skirt — sister door, not the rail hook. This is 820 Albee Rd W, not a Key marina tackle pin.
verifiedStory: Official about still names the bait counter (live and frozen) and the rod wall: Okuma, Redbone, Penn, Falcon, and Ricky Reds (Rick Murphy’s rods), plus Yo-Zuri, Rapala, and DOA. Jennie’s 9 Jan 2020 post dates the adjoining Casey Key Beach Shop to 2013 so the rest of the party could shop while bait is bagged. Official pages fetched this pass do not print a bait-shop founding year.
funFact: It's a two-in-one operation — a serious anglers' tackle shop right next to a beach-supply store, about two blocks from the sand.
currentUsefulDetail: Open Monday–Saturday 6am–6pm and Sunday 6am–5pm; call for live-bait availability on busy weekends. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's a small independent bait shop with early-evening closing, not a big-box outfitter — call ahead for live bait on busy weekends.

name: Red Barn Flea Market
hours: Full market Fri–Sun 9am–4pm (seasonal Wed Nov–Apr); free admission & parking
vibeCheck: A sprawling Bradenton flea market that's part treasure hunt, part farmers market, part food court — 600-plus booths across 145,000 square feet, with a big air-conditioned indoor section for hot days. Cheap, chaotic, and fun.
whyGo: The same family has run Red Barn since 1981: 145,000 square feet, more than 600 booths, 80,000 of them air-conditioned. Visit Sarasota posts the full market Friday–Sunday 9 a.m.–4 p.m., with seasonal Wednesdays November–April. Admission and parking are free.
bestFor: Bargain-hunters, souvenir-seekers, and cheap-produce shoppers. Not for anyone wanting polished boutiques or a quick in-and-out.
knownFor: Family-run since 1981; 600-plus booths, 80,000 sq ft of A/C
powerhouseProof: Official 1981 / 145,000 / 80,000 / 600-plus figures. Visit Sarasota: free admission and parking; full market Fri–Sun 9–4; seasonal Wednesday November–April. enjoyflorida.com repeats 600-plus vendor spaces.
insiderMove: Come Friday–Sunday (or a seasonal Wednesday) if you want the full 600-booth floor. Tuesday the plaza and the north-end produce stand can still be open. Use the 80,000-square-foot A/C hall when the lot is hot.
verifiedStory: Official copy: the same family has operated the Bradenton market since 1981, now 145,000 square feet with more than 600 booths and 80,000 square feet of air-conditioned indoor shopping plus an open-air produce stand. The operator splits “Plaza Only” from the “Entire Market.”
funFact: At 145,000 square feet and 600-plus booths it's one of the area's largest flea markets — and both admission and parking are free.
currentUsefulDetail: The full flea market runs Friday–Sunday 9am–4pm (with seasonal Wednesdays November–April); the front plaza shops keep some additional weekday hours. Free admission and parking. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's weekend-focused (Fri–Sun), much of it is outdoor (hot in summer), and vendor quality is hit-or-miss — this is a treasure hunt, not a tidy market. Some regulars note more empty booths than in years past.

name: St. Armands Circle
vibeCheck: An upscale open-air shopping-and-dining circle on St. Armands Key — boutiques, restaurants, and ice cream ringing a landscaped roundabout dotted with antique statues. A stroll-and-browse destination, not a quick errand.
whyGo: Ringling platted the shops around a park circle and opened it in 1926 with a parade over a causeway his elephants helped build. Almost 150 merchants still sit on that plan. Use the North Adams garage — first hour is free if you register the plate.
bestFor: Strollers, gift-shoppers, and diners who want an upscale open-air scene, ideally paired with a Lido Beach visit. Bargain-hunters and errand-runners will find it pricey.
knownFor: A 1926 Ringling shopping circle: streets radiate from a park, with Italian statuary from his collection.
powerhouseProof: St. Armands Circle Association: almost 150 merchants; North Adams garage $1/hour after a complimentary first hour with plate registration.
insiderMove: Skip circling for a street meter. North Adams garage is $1 an hour, first hour free after you register the plate. 186 free spaces sit on North and South Boulevard of the Presidents.
verifiedStory: Charles St. Amand bought 131.89 acres here in 1893 for $21.71. John Ringling bought the key in 1917. Causeway work began in 1925; circus elephants hauled the timbers. The causeway and the development opened in 1926.
funFact: The Circus Ring of Fame rings the circle with bronze wagon-wheel plaques honoring circus legends; the program was approved in 1986, held its first induction in April 1988, and now counts more than 150 inductees.
currentUsefulDetail: Paid parking is in effect 24 hours a day, every day (free only Sunday mornings and city holidays); most shops open around 10–11am and close between 6 and 10pm. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's upscale, and paid parking runs essentially around the clock — budget for both the shops and the meter. This is a destination for browsing and dining, not a quick practical errand stop.

name: Tervis Store
vibeCheck: The flagship store of Tervis, the made-in-Florida insulated-tumbler brand — walls of double-wall cups in licensed sports, college, and Disney designs, plus a build-your-own station. A gift-shop stop with hometown-brand pride.
whyGo: The Tervis store is at 928 South Tamiami Trail in Osprey, on the original plant site. Sarasota Magazine (August 2025) says Hosana Fieber and Rogan Donelly now own this shop as the brand's only walk-in retail door, and it is the only counter that replaces a damaged tumbler the same day. Official about still calls the plant a retail location.
bestFor: Gift shoppers, made-in-USA fans, sports and Disney fans, and families (the build-your-own is a hit with kids). Not a bargain outing — it's mostly full retail.
knownFor: Osprey plant-site Tervis store at 928 S Tamiami; same-day warranty walk-in
powerhouseProof: 928 S Tamiami Trail, Osprey; 941-966-8614. SM 2025: same-day warranty replacement only at this counter; mail-in elsewhere. Official about: lifetime guarantee; 1946 double-wall; 1967 Florida manufacturing. 2017 SM named The Lab at +$5 — not used as today’s price.
insiderMove: Navigate to 928 South Tamiami Trail. Bring a damaged tumbler here if you want a same-day walk-in replacement — SM 2025 says every other channel is mail-in. Do not treat the 2017 Lab $5 or those Lab hours as today’s custom desk. Official about still says “flagship”; this card does not.
verifiedStory: Official about: Cotter and Davis, 1946; Winslow manufacturing in Florida, 1967; Osprey plant now the retail location. SM Aug 2025: Fieber and Donelly own the Osprey shop; Tervis LLC (JV2) is the wholesale side; Fieber called this the only retail store. Official about still describes a Donelly-era map of multiple branded stores.
funFact: The name "Tervis" is a mash-up of its two inventors' last names — and every tumbler carries a lifetime guarantee, so they'll replace a cracked one.
currentUsefulDetail: This is the Osprey factory store (not Venice, despite common listings); it's generally open Monday–Saturday 10am–6pm and Sunday noon–5pm — call to confirm. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's in Osprey, not Venice, and it's mostly full retail pricing (the deals are in the clearance bin). The famous two-story giant tumbler landmark is at the North Venice headquarters, not this store.

name: Waterside Place
hours: Open-air district; hours vary by shop (Sunday Farmers' Market 10am–2pm)
vibeCheck: A newer waterfront shopping-and-dining district in Lakewood Ranch, wrapped around Kingfisher Lake — restaurants and shops with lake views, live music, a splash park, and the Sunday farmers market. Polished and family-friendly.
whyGo: Waterside Place is Lakewood Ranch's lakefront town center — not Main Street. The Sunday Farmers' Market runs 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. year-round on that waterfront. American Farmland Trust named it the No. 1 U.S. farmers market in 2025.
bestFor: A waterfront Sunday-morning outing, date-night dinner and drinks on the lake, and families (splash park, market Kids' Zone). Not for a quiet or historic-downtown feel — it's newer and can get busy.
knownFor: Lakefront LWR town center; Sunday market 10–2; AFT No. 1 U.S. 2025
powerhouseProof: Official and Visit Sarasota: Sunday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. year-round; 100-plus vendors; AFT 2025 national first. Florida Provisions’ operator deal is written as Sunday market hours on the Waterside page.
foodMove: Dining anchors include Deep Lagoon seafood, Korê Steakhouse, and Good Liquid Brewing, with Duck Donuts for a sweet stop.
insiderMove: Sunday at 10 a.m. is the market — on the Waterside lakefront, not on Main Street. Visit Sarasota puts kids’ workshops in The Yard next to Good Liquid Brewing. First-Friday Music on Main is the other district.
verifiedStory: Official October 3, 2025 press: the year-round Sunday market at Waterside Place was named the No. 1 U.S. farmers market by American Farmland Trust, topping about 1,300 markets, and also took Florida. Visit Sarasota (Nov 30, 2025) repeats the Sunday 10–2 clock, the 100-plus vendor count, and the Waterside pin. Main Street is a different LWR street.
funFact: Its Sunday farmers market was voted the single best in the entire United States in 2025 — after two prior years as Florida's #1.
currentUsefulDetail: An open-air district, so hours vary by shop and restaurant; the signature Sunday Farmers' Market runs 10am–2pm year-round along the lakefront. Verified 2026-07-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It's newer and can feel busy and commercial on Sunday market mornings, when parking gets tight. It's a master-planned waterfront center, not a historic downtown.

name: ICON Park
hours: Free to walk; attractions separately ticketed — The Orlando Eye from $29.99, SEA LIFE and Madame Tussauds from $33.99 each
vibeCheck: An open-air entertainment destination built around The Orlando Eye, with a wax museum, an aquarium and a slingshot clustered at its feet, and more restaurants than most malls.
whyGo: You can stack three genuinely different attractions into one afternoon on a single combo ticket, then eat without moving the car.
bestFor: Families and first-time visitors who want variety in one place. Skip it if you would rather have one deep experience than a sampler.
knownFor: The Orlando Eye, SEA LIFE Orlando Aquarium, Madame Tussauds, the Museum of Illusions and the Orlando SlingShot.
powerhouseProof: SEA LIFE Orlando has Florida's only 360° ocean tunnel.
foodMove: Gordon Ramsay's Fish Chips and Shake Shack cover fast casual; Yard House and Blake Shelton's Ole Red handle a sit-down.
drinkMove: Tin Roof: A Live Music Joint and Sugar Factory Orlando are the drink stops.
insiderMove: Do not buy attractions one at a time. The Three Attraction Combo puts SEA LIFE, Madame Tussauds and The Orlando Eye together starting at $49 per adult, against $33.99 each bought separately.
funFact: The Orlando SlingShot catapults riders 450 feet into the air, going 0 to 100 in less than 2 seconds.
currentUsefulDetail: Blue Man Group starts at $59.00 per adult; the Two Attraction Combo starts at $39.
watchOut: Almost everything is separately ticketed. Walking the park is free, the attractions are not, and a family doing four of them adds up fast.

name: Scenic Boat Tour

Adults $18.78 + $1.22 tax = $20.00; children 2–11 $9.38 + $0.62 = $10.00. Closed Christmas Day (19 Aug about/home). Six pontoon boats. Groups larger than 18 and wheelchair seats call ahead. Wikipedia Winter Park this pass cites Scenic Boat Tours and says boat tours are available on the chain; it does not print a founding year. Kraft Azalea Park Wikipedia this pass dates the garden — not the boat — to 1938 and calls the tour an 18-passenger trip. Do not use the park’s year as a second founding source.

address: 312 East Morse Blvd. Winter Park, FL 32789

name: Mead Botanical Garden
hours: Open daily 8:00 a.m. to dusk; admission free
vibeCheck: Forty-seven acres of Winter Park left mostly to itself — hiking trails, a creek, a boardwalk under tall pine trees, and a pond with turtles and wading birds.
whyGo: Mead Botanical Garden sits at Garden Drive and Denning Drive in Winter Park. Official history dates the dedication to January 14, 1940, and the March 31, 1953, deed to the city that still requires a botanical garden. Home copy says 47 free acres; the visit page fetched this pass printed 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a walk rather than an attraction, and families with young naturalists. Not a manicured display garden.
knownFor: 1940 Winter Park garden at Garden Dr and Denning Dr; free; 47-acre home copy
powerhouseProof: Free admission. Visit page this pass: 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; entrance Garden Dr at Denning Dr; leashed dogs. About: dawn to dusk. Home: 47 acres, trails, creek, boardwalk, greenhouse, butterfly garden, pond.
insiderMove: Garden Drive is easy to miss — official visit says so. The gate is Garden at Denning. Dogs stay leashed. Personal photos without props are fine; a paid shoot needs the city’s open-air permit. Do not promise the live-card Saturday 9:00 yoga / 10:30 tai chi clock; about names the programs, not those times. Confirm hours: visit printed 8–7 today; about still says dawn to dusk.
verifiedStory: After T.L. Mead died in 1936, Jack Connery and Rollins Professor of Books Dr. Edwin Grover pushed a garden in his name. Dedication 14 January 1940. Deeded to the City of Winter Park 31 March 1953 with a botanical-garden restriction. History page starts the land at about 50 acres; about now says 48; home says 47.
funFact: The Azalea Lodge hosts Candlelight concerts by the glow of actual candlelight.
currentUsefulDetail: Recurring programs include Yoga in the Garden, Tai Chi in the Garden, a Sound Bath, and the Great Duck Derby.
watchOut: It closes at dusk rather than a fixed hour, so a late-afternoon visit is shorter than you think.

name: Harry P. Leu Gardens
hours: Summer Hours: 9 a.m. - 6 p.m., Thursdays: 9 a.m. - 8 p.m.
vibeCheck: Fifty acres of camellias and old trees sitting three miles from downtown, quiet enough that the loudest thing is usually the birds.
whyGo: It is the rare botanical garden with a house museum attached, so you get a serious plant collection and an 1888 home in one walk.
bestFor: Anyone who wants green space without leaving the city, and history-minded visitors who will actually tour the house.
knownFor: A renowned camellia collection across 50 acres, plus the Historic Leu House Museum.
powerhouseProof: It is marking its 65th anniversary, and the Leu House is on the National Register.
insiderMove: Come December through March when the camellias are actually blooming, and take a Thursday, when the gardens stay open to 8 p.m. and there is live music June through September.
verifiedStory: The Historic Leu House Museum dates to 1888 and is a National Register site.
funFact: The camellia display runs December to March, when most of Florida has nothing else blooming.
currentUsefulDetail: Legacy In Bloom runs through May 31, 2026, with live music on Thursdays June through September.
watchOut: Last entry is one hour before closing, and some exhibits keep shorter hours than the gardens.

name: Orlando Science Center

vibeCheck: Loud, hands-on and unapologetically for kids, with live demos running through the day and laser shows after dark.

bestFor: Families with school-age kids and students. Less compelling if you want a quiet afternoon.

insiderMove: Skip Wednesday unless official pages say it is an OCPS break. Buy online — onsite is the higher tier. Ask for Science For All at the desk if you have EBT or WIC; it is daytime general admission, not Science Night Live. Do not plan on Friday/Saturday lasers — Stellar Nights ended 8 August 2026 even though the live card still stores that line.

Same campaign page still says “over the last 63 years.” KidsTown finished October 2016; Hive makerspace and Flight Lab 2018. Official pages fetched this pass do not reprint the 777 East Princeton street line in the visit body; the live card still stores it.
currentUsefulDetail: Check the Daily Calendar for schedule updates.
watchOut: Weekends draw crowds, and Stellar Nights in particular fills up.

name: Gatorland
hours: 10 AM - 6 PM daily, rain or shine
vibeCheck: Old-Florida roadside attraction that never modernised itself into blandness, with alligators, zip lines and shows running all day.
whyGo: It is the cheap, unfussy counterweight to the big parks down the road, and the zip line runs over the alligators rather than past them.
bestFor: Families who want animals over rides, and anyone tired of paying theme-park prices. Skip it if you want air conditioning.
knownFor: Alligator shows, ziplining over the breeding marsh, and animal exhibits.
powerhouseProof: It has been running for over 70 years, which in Orlando means it predates the theme parks entirely.
insiderMove: Buy online before you go rather than at the gate, and check their social media the morning of, since weather closes parts of the park.
watchOut: It is largely outdoors in Florida heat, and peak seasons and holidays get crowded.
address: 14501 S. Orange Blossom Trail, Orlando, Florida 32837

name: Orlando Museum of Art
hours: Extended hours on third Thursday of every month for Access for All at OM°A (10 am to 8 pm)
vibeCheck: A serious collection in a city that does not get credit for having one, quiet on weekdays and genuinely busy on free Thursdays.
whyGo: You can stand in front of an Andy Warhol and a Kerry James Marshall without leaving Orlando, and once a month you can do it for free.
bestFor: Anyone who wants an afternoon that is not a theme park. Families are well served, with reduced admission for ages 6-17, students, seniors and visitors with disabilities.
knownFor: American art of the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries, art of the Ancient Americas, and works by Richard Diebenkorn, Kerry James Marshall, Nick Cave and Andy Warhol.
powerhouseProof: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums since 1971, a standing only a small share of American museums hold.
insiderMove: Go on the third Thursday, when Access for All at OM°A runs 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. free, with performances and interactive activities. It is the single best-value art afternoon in the city.
verifiedStory: It began in 1924 as the Orlando Art Association, a small gallery where artists met to display and critique each other's work.
funFact: The permanent collection runs to over 3,300 works, spanning Contemporary Art, American Art to 1945, the Art of the Ancient Americas and African Art.
currentUsefulDetail: Tickets are available online or at the front desk, and the third Thursday of each month is free.
watchOut: Weekends and peak tourist season are the busiest times to come.

name: Mennello Museum of American Art
hours: Tuesday - Saturday 10:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., Sunday 12 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.
vibeCheck: Small enough to see properly in an hour, which is the point, with rotating shows and a pollinator garden out back.
whyGo: The Mennello is the City of Orlando museum at 900 East Princeton Street, in the Howard Phillips house on Lake Formosa. Official history dates it to November 1998 for the Earl Cunningham collection. Tuesday through Saturday the clock is 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; Sunday opens at noon.
bestFor: Anyone who bounces off big museums, and families looking for a short cultural stop. Not for a full afternoon.
knownFor: November 1998 Orlando art museum; Earl Cunningham collection; Howard Phillips house on Lake Formosa
powerhouseProof: Tue–Sat 10:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Sun noon–4:30 p.m.; closed Monday. Adults $8; 60+ $5; kids 6–17 $3; under 6 and military families free. Sculpture garden always open. Free adjacent lot. Smithsonian American Art Museum Affiliate. Noguchi *Metal the Mirror* Aug 28, 2026–Feb 28, 2027.
insiderMove: Go Tuesday–Saturday at 10:30, or Sunday at noon. Second Sunday is Free Family Funday — tours at 12:30, 1:30, and 2:30 p.m. The sculpture garden does not wait on a ticket. Park in the free lot beside the museum; the Science Center garage is $5. SunRail is the weekday station at 500 East Rollins.
verifiedStory: Official About Us: established November 1998, City of Orlando, Howard Phillips house, Earl Cunningham permanent collection. Founders page names Marilyn Logsdon Mennello and Michael A. Mennello (Michael died in 2020) and traces Cunningham collecting to the early 1980s — that is collecting, not the museum’s open date. Wikipedia (secondary) prints November 22, 1998. The live card’s “Ralph Mennello / 1982” line is wrong.
funFact: Luca Molnar's mural in the Pollinator Garden blends historical photographs with decorative pattern.
currentUsefulDetail: Current shows are 'Luca Molnar: Worker Bees' and 'Our Orlando: Tasanee Durrett, Martha Jo Mahoney & Mado Smith'.
watchOut: Closed Mondays and major holidays, and it is genuinely small, so pair it with Leu Gardens up the road.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Mary, Queen of the Universe
hours: Daily; check the shrine schedule for Mass times
vibeCheck: A working pilgrimage site rather than a neighbourhood parish, so it carries the hush of a shrine with tourists filing through.
whyGo: It is a designated shrine minutes from the parks, holding a Shroud of Turin replica and Timothy Schmalz sculptures.
bestFor: Visitors who want Mass while travelling, and anyone drawn to religious art. Not a stop for the merely curious in a hurry.
knownFor: Its shrine status, the Shroud of Turin replica, and Timothy Schmalz sculptures.
powerhouseProof: It is a designated National Shrine with a Shroud of Turin exhibit, not a parish church.
insiderMove: Come outside Mass times if you want to see the Shroud replica and the Schmalz sculptures without moving through a congregation.
funFact: It is not a parish church at all, but a dedicated pilgrimage destination.
watchOut: Peak seasons draw crowds and parking is limited.

name: STK Steakhouse
vibeCheck: A modern steakhouse in the heart of Disney Springs with live DJs and a lively atmosphere — closer to a night out than a quiet dinner.
whyGo: Signature steaks and elevated cocktails without leaving Disney Springs, in a room that deliberately feels different from everything around it.
bestFor: Adults who want a real steakhouse inside the Disney Springs bubble. Not the pick for a quiet table or an early night with kids.
knownFor: Signature steaks, elevated cocktails and live DJs.
powerhouseProof: It sits in the heart of Disney Springs, one of Orlando's most popular dining destinations.
foodMove: Signature steaks are the point.
drinkMove: Elevated cocktails, with live DJs running alongside.
insiderMove: Book ahead through the venue's own reservation form rather than walking up — this is a Disney Springs room on a Disney Springs schedule.
watchOut: Live DJs and a lively atmosphere mean volume — this is not a quiet dinner.

name: Old Town
vibeCheck: A nostalgic entertainment district in the heart of Kissimmee — shops, dining, rides and a weekly car show, all walkable and free to enter.
whyGo: Old Town is the Kissimmee entertainment district at 5770 West Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway. Official hours run 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and to 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Friday muscle cars start at 3 p.m.; Saturday classics start at 1 p.m.; both cruises kick off at 8:30 on the bricks.
bestFor: Families and car people who want an unticketed evening. Less good if you want a single headline attraction.
knownFor: Friday 3 p.m. muscle and Saturday 1 p.m. classic cruises at 5770 W. Irlo Bronson
powerhouseProof: Sun–Thu 11 a.m.–10 p.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–11 p.m. Friday muscle 3 p.m. / cruise 8:30. Saturday classic 1 p.m. / cruise 8:30. Wednesday bike 6–10 p.m. First Sunday import show. Show and cruise printed at no cost. Security (407) 225-0553.
foodMove: Hamburger Mary's Bar & Grille serves lunch and dinner Monday through Friday and brunch on Saturdays and Sundays.
insiderMove: Friday, be on Trophy Row at 3 p.m.; Saturday, 1 p.m. The cruise is 8:30 either night. Cruisers enter from Highway 192 under the east Jukebox signs — bricks are permission-only. Call security at (407) 225-0553 for lost-and-found; Enjoy Florida still prints (407) 396-4888.
verifiedStory: Official car-show page: “nearly 35 years,” no founding year. Wikipedia (secondary) prints December 1986 and an April 2019 re-opening with an 86-foot Ferris wheel. Contact places the district one mile east of I-4 exit 67 at 5770 W. Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway.
funFact: Hamburger Mary's brings its classic bingo, trivia and Broadway brunch to the district.
currentUsefulDetail: Hamburger Mary's Bar & Grille is now open.
watchOut: Rides and attractions are individually paid, so a full evening adds up even though walking in is free.

name: Keke's Breakfast Cafe
vibeCheck: A breakfast-and-brunch cafe that does one meal properly and closes before dinner — the local answer to a hotel buffet.
whyGo: Breakfast is the whole menu rather than a section of it, and you can order online and skip the wait instead of standing in a queue.
bestFor: Families and anyone who wants a real breakfast before a park day. Not a dinner option.
knownFor: Breakfast and brunch favorites, now serving in seven states.
powerhouseProof: Keke's is now serving in seven states.

insiderMove: Order online and skip the wait — the queue is the main cost of eating here, and the app removes it.
currentUsefulDetail: The $5 Kid's Meal Deal runs Monday–Friday with an adult entrée purchase, now through August 28.
watchOut: It is a breakfast cafe, so plan around its hours rather than turning up hungry in the evening.

name: Bubba Gump Shrimp Co.
vibeCheck: A Forrest Gump-themed seafood restaurant at Universal CityWalk, decorated like the movie's Alabama setting and entirely unembarrassed about it.
whyGo: It is family-friendly, open to walk-ins, and the movie memorabilia is real — script pages, storyboards and costumes rather than generic props.

insiderMove: It is open to walk ins, which at CityWalk is worth more than the menu — no reservation, no queue app.
watchOut: It is a themed chain restaurant at a theme-park entertainment district — priced and paced accordingly.

name: The Florida Mall
vibeCheck: A full-line Simon mall rather than an outlet — department stores and designer names under one roof, and open when the parks are.
whyGo: It is the everything-mall: Coach Outlet, Michael Kors, Burberry, Nike and adidas in one trip, without outlet-mall driving.

watchOut: It closes at 8:00PM, earlier than the outlet centers nearby, so an after-park visit needs planning.

name: Orlando Vineland Premium Outlets
vibeCheck: The luxury end of Orlando outlet shopping — designer names at outlet pricing, open an hour later than the full-line malls.
whyGo: Designer brands at outlet prices, and it stays open to 9:00PM, so it absorbs the evening after a park day.

insiderMove: Sign up for Simon+ first — cash back and perks on outlet pricing is the closest thing to stacking discounts here.
watchOut: Outlet pricing draws crowds, and the 9:00PM close is the busiest stretch after the parks empty.

name: Winter Park Village
vibeCheck: An open-air lifestyle center under palm trees and oak shaded walkways, just north of Orlando — a stroll rather than a mall trip.
whyGo: Winter Park Village is the lifestyle center at 510 Orlando Avenue. Official contact prints that street and does not publish a walkability rank.
bestFor: Anyone who wants an unhurried evening out. Not the pick for outlet pricing or one-stop department shopping.
knownFor: Lifestyle center at 510 Orlando Ave with 20-screen Regal Winter Park Village & RPX
powerhouseProof: 510 Orlando Avenue, Winter Park, FL 32789. Regal Winter Park Village & RPX: 20-theater stadium at 510 N. Orlando Avenue; (844) 462-7342. Official home: shops, restaurants, cinema on one pad.
foodMove: The dining runs from casual to gourmet dinner.
insiderMove: Navigate to 510 Orlando Avenue. The movie is Regal Winter Park Village & RPX — 20 screens — not a single art house. Do not repeat “most walkable”; official contact never prints that rank. Live card still has no address; official contact does.

currentUsefulDetail: Live music and seasonal events run through the year.
watchOut: It is a lifestyle center, so the retail is boutique-scale — go elsewhere for a full department store.

name: Lake Buena Vista Factory Stores
vibeCheck: A compact outlet center off State Rd 535 with its own free shuttle — the outlet you go to when you do not want to drive.
whyGo: The Free Shopping Shuttle makes over 60 stops, so this is the outlet center you can reach without a car or a parking fight.
bestFor: Visitors without a car, and anyone who wants outlet pricing without the drive. Less good if you want the designer end.
knownFor: Outlet shopping with a free shuttle and an on-site resort.
powerhouseProof: The Free Shopping Shuttle runs over 60 stops.
insiderMove: Check the shuttle schedule before you book a ride — with over 60 stops it very likely already serves your hotel.
currentUsefulDetail: Deals and coupons are published on the site before you go.
watchOut: Sunday hours are shorter — 11am-7pm against 10am-9pm the rest of the week.

name: SeaWorld Orlando
vibeCheck: Half marine park, half coaster park — orcas and a shark tunnel on one side, record-breaking rides on the other.
whyGo: You get genuine animal encounters and serious coasters on one ticket, which no other Orlando park offers.
bestFor: Families mixing animals with thrill rides. Visitors uneasy about marine mammals in human care should read up first.
knownFor: Dolphin Cove, Orca Underwater Viewing, Shark Encounter, Sesame Street Land and its roller coasters.
powerhouseProof: Fewer than 10% of the approximately 2,800 animal exhibitors licensed by the USDA have met AZA standards, and SeaWorld is one of them.
foodMove: Red, White, and BBQ runs weekends July 4 to August 23, 2026, with BBQ from the most iconic regions across the US.
drinkMove: The Fireworks and Drone Show VIP Viewing adds a happy hour with premium tapas and cocktails on the waterfront patio at Lakeside Grill.
insiderMove: Go late in summer: Electric Ocean runs select dates now to September 7, 2026, and staying past dark is how you get the fireworks and drone show.
funFact: With more than 43,000 rescues to date, SeaWorld is one of the largest marine animal rescue organizations in the world.
currentUsefulDetail: Baby Shark at SeaWorld runs now to September 7. Active-duty military get FREE tickets.
watchOut: Annual Pass perks like free parking do not extend to single-day tickets, and the up-close animal tours and Quick Queue passes are all paid add-ons.

name: Brohard Paw Park/Beach
hours: City 7 a.m.–dusk; county 6 a.m.–10 p.m. Follow posted signs.
vibeCheck: A working dog yard that opens onto Gulf sand. Waste-bag stations, showers, and a clear line on the beach between dogs and the people-only park south of you.
whyGo: This is the only stretch of Sarasota County sand that lets a dog reach the Gulf. You walk a fenced play yard, then a posted dog beach.
bestFor: People who want their dog in the Gulf. Skip it if you want a lifeguarded family swim, or if a pack of off-leash dogs is not your morning.
knownFor: Off-leash dogs on a signed slice of Venice beach, plus a fenced yard, showers, and drinking fountains for people and dogs.
powerhouseProof: Every other county beach turns a dog away at the sand. Here the yard opens onto the Gulf, and the next park south is the human-only contrast.
insiderMove: Read the signs for where the dog beach ends. South Brohard, immediately south, is people only.
verifiedStory: The city owns the park; the county maintains it. In 2021 the city restated the rule in writing: dogs stay welcome here, off-leash on the beach inside the posted area, while Maxine Barritt next door allows leashed dogs only on paths and parking — not on that park's sand.
funFact: South Brohard, the people-only park next door, is named for Smyth Brohard, Venice mayor from 1958 to 1971.
currentUsefulDetail: Beach portion temporarily closed as of city update 12 Aug 2026 for Venice Shore Protection Project. Official listings split the street number: city/county 1850 Harbor Drive S; Visit Sarasota / Atlas pin 1600 Harbor Drive S. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Hours conflict city vs county; no lifeguard on this stretch; beach may be closed during remaining construction / outfall work. County lists a restroom; Visit Venice says use Maxine Barritt next door.

name: Palma Sola Causeway
vibeCheck: Bayside sand along a busy two-lane, picnic space, and boat trailers. You hear traffic as much as water.
whyGo: You stop on the bay, not the Gulf — a roadside picnic and a kayak put-in on the drive to Anna Maria Island.
bestFor: A short bay stop, a picnic, or a paddle. Skip it if you want Gulf surf, a guard, or a full-service beach.
knownFor: Palma Sola Bay on both sides of Manatee Avenue. County boat ramp. A marked blueway launch toward Perico Island.
powerhouseProof: Holmes Beach and Coquina are Gulf parks with towers and lots. This is the bayside pause before the island bridge — water on both shoulders, no guard, no café.
insiderMove: Put in anywhere along the causeway, both sides of the road. The 5.25-mile paddle around Perico is the county's own short trip, about two hours.
funFact: County paddle notes put the Perico Island loop at 5.25 miles and about two hours from this causeway.
currentUsefulDetail: PALMA SOLA SOUTH tested Poor (enterococcus 500) on 10 Aug 2026 — check Florida Healthy Beaches before you swim. Refresh before display.
watchOut: There is no lifeguard. Flags fly on the island towers, not here. The road is SR 64; you share the shoulder with traffic headed to the island.

name: Service Club Park
vibeCheck: A long wooden walk through picnic shade, then open Gulf sand. More park than scene.
whyGo: A 370-foot boardwalk, rebuilt in 2018, walks you from a picnic park to a quieter slice of Venice beach — restrooms, showers, and a playground behind you.
bestFor: A family picnic that ends in the Gulf, or anyone who wants shade tables on the walkover. Skip it if you need a guard tower or a dog on the sand.
knownFor: Covered picnic tables on the way to the Gulf, sand volleyball, grills, and a walkway the city built with Sertoma, Lions, and Kiwanis.
powerhouseProof: Venice Beach has the lifeguards. Brohard, down Harbor Drive, has the dogs. This one is the club-built boardwalk with shade tables on the walk to the sand.
insiderMove: Treat this as the picnic-and-swim park, not the guarded Venice Beach lot. Bring the grill food; there is no concession on the city page.
verifiedStory: Area service clubs — Sertoma, Lions, and Kiwanis — built this park with volunteer time and money. The city still names them. The 370-foot walkway was renovated in 2018.
funFact: The walkway is 370 feet — renovated in 2018 — and the city still credits Sertoma, Lions, and Kiwanis for the park itself.
currentUsefulDetail: Inside the 2026 Venice Shore Protection Project area (city FAQ). Confirm access. Healthy Beaches SERVICE CLUB BEACH last sampled 27 Jul 2026 as of this pass. Refresh before display.
watchOut: No lifeguard. Construction / outfall work may still affect the sand.

name: Bridge Tender Inn
hours: Daily 11am–11:30pm (FAQ still says 11:30am start); no reservations
vibeCheck: A Packers-bar and dockside grille on historic Bridge Street — the kitchen sits on the street, the T-shaped dock and tiki sit across Bay Drive South on Sarasota Bay. Loud, casual, no reservations.
whyGo: You eat and watch the game in a sports bar that has been on this corner since 1989, then walk across the street to drink on the bay. Arrive by car, bike, or boat (they post mile marker 49).
bestFor: Sports-and-seafood people who will wait for a table and want dogs on the patio. Not for anyone who needs a reservation or a quiet room.
knownFor: No-reservation sports bar and a separate dockside bar across Bay Drive — eighteen TVs, Packers colors, and a T-shaped dock on the bay.
powerhouseProof: Opened in 1989; owner Fred Bartizal; the general manager, Sue, has been there more than twenty-five years.
foodMove: Anna Maria Island's listing calls out the Grouper Reuben, Baja fish tacos, and Shrimpcargot; Sarasota Magazine keeps coming back for the ribeye steak sandwich with caramelized onions and provolone. Official menu page is blank — confirm at the table.
drinkMove: A tropical cocktail at the Dockside Bar across Bay Drive, where the water view actually is.
insiderMove: They do not take reservations. Grab a drink and wait. Find the building by the surfboard leaning on a snowmobile by the tiki. Indoor dining room is Friday–Saturday only in the off-season.
verifiedStory: Established in 1989 as Bridge Tender Inn & Dockside Bar. The restaurant and the open-air bar are separate parcels across Bay Drive South, tied by a unity of title after a 2001 city land swap.
funFact: The landmark they tell you to look for is a surfboard leaning on a snowmobile by the tiki.
currentUsefulDetail: Official contact page: open 7 days, 11am–11:30pm, no reservations. FAQ still says 11:30am start. Take-out days vary — call 941-778-4849. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: Expect a wait and a walk across Bay Drive to reach the water seats. Inside the bar you need shoes and a shirt; the patio is the pet-friendly side.

name: Casey Key Fish House
vibeCheck: An Old Florida seafood house on the Intracoastal at Blackburn Point — a rambling dining room over the water and a chickee-style tiki a few feet from the swing bridge.
whyGo: The Osprey fish house still prints the Gulf plates that built the room: conch fritters fried golden with tartar, a grouper sandwich you pick blackened, grilled, or fried, and New England clam chowder. This is the fish house, not Casey Key Marina.
bestFor: Flip-flop seafood lunches and boat-in afternoons. Not a special-occasion dining room.
knownFor: Its conch fritters, grouper sandwich, and New England clam chowder
powerhouseProof: Official take-out PDF dated 09.30.25 still names New England Clam Chowder, Conch Fritters with tartar, and a Grouper Sandwich blackened, grilled, or fried. Same sheet types 175 feet of deep-water dockage and Marker 32. Homepage: Casey Key Fish House and Tiki Bar.
foodMove: Sarasota Magazine's longtime orders: baby calamari with housemade marinara, and Willie Tia's Best Bouillabaisse (lobster tail, mussels, shrimp, scallops, and grouper in Pernod broth, market price).
drinkMove: Start at the chickee-style tiki on the Intracoastal. The magazine still names longtime bartender Skeeter.
insiderMove: Come by water to Marker 32 if that’s the plan — dockage is on the official sheet. Do not confuse this pin with Casey Key Marina. The live HTML menu is pictures; pull the house take-out PDF if you want named plates.
verifiedStory: Owner Jimmy Von Hubertz’s Osprey fish house (opened 2000; manager Joe Zax) still bills itself “Old Florida at its Best.” After Milton wrecked the equipment, the house came back with the same Gulf board. The official take-out PDF — not the image-only HTML menu — is the receipt.
funFact: The tiki sits just feet from the Blackburn Point swing bridge, so you eat while the span opens for boat traffic.
currentUsefulDetail: Official hours: open 7 days from 11:30 a.m.; close time seasonal. Phone 941-966-1901. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: Closing time is seasonal, so call before a late dinner. Weekend tiki nights fill; dress is Bermuda shorts, not jackets.

name: Dakin Dairy Farm
hours: Cafe Mon–Fri 9am–5pm, Sat 9am–2pm; market Sat to 4pm; Sun closed
vibeCheck: A working Myakka City dairy where lunch happens at Pete's Place — milk bottled on the same property, ice cream after, tractors moving past the picnic porch.
whyGo: Dakin Dairy Farms bottles its own grass-fed milk on the Myakka City farm and scoops farm-fresh ice cream and specialty milkshakes at the cafe. Official product pages still name cheddar, Cajun, jalapeño, and Boursin-style cheese curds from the same herd.
bestFor: Families who want a farm afternoon more than a dinner out. Closed Sunday; no alcohol, no pets.
knownFor: On-farm bottled milk, farm ice cream, and cheese curds
powerhouseProof: Official contact: 30771 Betts Rd., Myakka City, FL 34251. Contact clock: Monday–Friday 9AM–5PM; Saturday 9AM–4PM; Sunday CLOSED. Official cafe: lunch Monday–Friday 9 am–5 pm and Saturdays 9am–2pm. Farm market: 9–5 Monday–Friday, 9–4 Saturday; closed Sunday. Cafe rules: no outside food or drinks; no alcoholic beverages; no pets; stay in designated public areas; shoes and shirt required. Pavilion rental: 941-322-2802 x303.
foodMove: Pulled-pork sandwich with slaw and their cheddar or pepper jack, or the chicken-salad croissant. Finish with farm ice cream. Prices on the cafe page go stale — read the board.
drinkMove: There is no bar. Get a milkshake or ice cream at Dakin Moofè.
insiderMove: Eat before 2 p.m. on Saturday if the meal is Pete's Place — the market stays to 4. Sunday is closed. Leave the dog at home. Official news calls the cafe Moofe; the cafe page still says Pete's Place; do not expect one sign. Confirm the lunch board on the counter — Observer May 2025 and the farm-market page still say food is coming, while `/cafe/` still types pulled pork. Stay inside marked public areas — this is a working dairy.
verifiedStory: Official homepage this pass: "Sustainable farming since 1973"; "one of the last remaining 150 dairy farms in Florida"; "The Dakin family has been milking cows in Manatee County, Florida since 1973"; "From milking the cows to the production and bottling, it all takes place on our Manatee County farm"; whole, skim, and chocolate milk; cheese curds, heavy cream, half and half; kosher-certified natural milk. name: Linger Lodge Restaurant & Bar
vibeCheck: A Braden River lodge where taxidermy watches you eat — squirrels playing basketball, jackalopes, a thirteen-foot gator — on screened decks over blackwater.
whyGo: Linger Lodge Restaurant is the Braden River taxidermy dining room Frank Gamsky started filling in 1968, after the Parvin family's 1945 fish camp. Official about-us still names fried alligator bites, fresh frog legs, and the Linger Lodge Bloody Mary; the house menu PDF prices a River Sampler Platter of fried green tomatoes, frog legs, and gator bites.
bestFor: Anyone who wants Old Florida more than a waterfront chain — gator, frog legs, smoked meat. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
knownFor: Gamsky taxidermy room — fried alligator bites, frog legs, Linger Lodge Bloody Mary
powerhouseProof: Official contact: 7116 85th Street Court East, Bradenton, FL 34202; Wed–Sun 11:30 a.m.–9 p.m.; Mon–Tue closed. Official restaurant-home: Happy Hour Wed–Fri 4–7; Trivia Thu 6:30–8; karaoke Fri 6–9; live Sat 6–9 and Sun noon–3; reserve at (941) 755-2757 or restaurant@lingerlodge.com. Official about-us: fried “alligator bites”; fresh frog legs; Linger Lodge Bloody Mary; cocktails Linger Lizard, Swamp Water, River Otter. Official menu PDF (Feb 2024 scan): Alligator Bites $20 (fried, grilled, or blackened); Fresh Frog Legs $16; River Sampler Platter $24 (fried green tomatoes, frog legs, local gator bites); Braden River Platter $30 (catfish, frog legs, local alligator); Florida Grouper market price; River Bottom Pie $12. Atlas still prints 7205.
foodMove: Alligator bites if you want the house wild card; the River Sampler (fried green tomatoes, alligator, frog legs) or River Platter (alligator, frog legs, catfish) for the full lodge plate. River Bottom Pie for dessert — Oreo crumbs, coffee ice cream, fudge.
drinkMove: A Bloody Mary is on their own specialties list. Happy hour Wednesday–Friday 4–7.
insiderMove: Reserve at (941) 755-2757 — they print phone or email, not a web widget. Do not come Monday or Tuesday. Official contact is 7116 85th Street Court East; the atlas pin still says 7205. If the mounted animals are too much, official copy gives two screened river decks. Treat Observer’s 2022 Lewis purchase as Observer, not official history.
verifiedStory: Official restaurant history: Parvin family, 1945, two-story log cabin on 100 acres; cabin burns late 1950s; Frank and Elaine Gamsky buy in 1968 (Frank, a veterinarian, starts the taxidermy); Hartl Family buys in 2016; 2022 is the finished RV-park renovation. Official history does not print Rita Lewis. Your Observer (20 Aug 2025, Marty Fugate) says Rita Lewis started in the kitchen, rose to general manager, and bought the place in 2022; that page also names alligator bites, frog legs, a River Platter, a River Sampler, and River Bottom Pie. Official /s/Menu returned 404 this pass. Official /s/Linger-Lodge-Menus is a scanned PDF (Squarespace timestamp 12 Feb 2024) whose visible pages type Alligator Bites, Fresh Frog Legs, River Sampler Platter, Braden River Platter, and River Bottom Pie — matching the Observer plate names, not inventing new ones. Official about-us still names the Jackalope, Alaskan Fur Fish, and Walking Catfish on the walls.
funFact: A wooden plaque in the house reads "Linger Longer" — Lewis says people stay because the river makes them slow down.
currentUsefulDetail: Official hours: Wednesday–Sunday 11:30am–9pm; closed Monday and Tuesday. Official street number is 7116 85th Street Court East; Google/Atlas lists 7205 — same riverside complex as the RV park. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It sits at the end of Linger Lodge Road behind a shopping center — follow the ranch-road directions. The dining room is full of mounted animals.

bestFor: Casual drinks and weekend breakfast on the sand. Skip it if you want quiet or a reservation — the line moves, but it is a line.
knownFor: Rum runner, Rachel sandwich, and coconut shrimp

name: Dry Dock Waterfront Grill
vibeCheck: A south-Longboat bayfront grill — second-story windows on Sarasota Bay, a dockside patio under palms, and boat slips at marker 6.
whyGo: Dry Dock plates locally caught Florida grouper — a kaiser sandwich, Citrus Grouper in orange-juice cream, and Grouper Bites — from a second-story room that looks across Sarasota Bay at Ca' d'Zan. Eric and Cindy Hammersand opened it May 1, 1989; Gecko's bought it in 2015 and kept the name.
bestFor: A Longboat seafood lunch or sunset dinner when you want the bay, not St. Armands. Families use the patio and lawn.
knownFor: Florida grouper on a kaiser and Citrus Grouper
powerhouseProof: 412 Gulf of Mexico Drive, Longboat Key, FL 34228; (941) 383-0102. Official footer this pass: Sun–Thurs 11 a.m.–9 p.m.; Fri & Sat 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m.; to-go 11 a.m.–4 p.m., last pickup 4:30 p.m.; Marker 6 via boat. Official menu this pass also lists Kickin' Grouper sandwich $31 (blackened local grouper, pepperjack) and Florida Grouper entrée $42. Visit Sarasota waterfront: second-story Sarasota Bay room; boats to Zwick's Channel at Marker 6. Visit Sarasota boat-up: hidden from cars on Longboat Key; Ca' D'Zan at The Ringling. Sarasota Magazine waterfront list this pass names the Ringling museum / New College sightline and the lobster roll, not the grouper sandwich. SM 2018 water-views still flags the Gulf-caught grouper sandwich and red snapper from the dockside patio.
foodMove: The Florida grouper sandwich — Visit Sarasota's house specialty — or the lobster roll Sarasota Magazine prefers. Grouper bites to start.
drinkMove: A glass on the dockside patio looking east across the bay — you face the mainland and The Ringling, not the Gulf.
insiderMove: Arrive by boat at marker 6 in Zwick's Channel. By car, Visit Sarasota notes the room is easy to miss from Gulf of Mexico Drive. Official hours this pass print Fri–Sat to 9:30 p.m.; Sarasota Magazine's listing still prints Monday–Sunday 11 a.m.–9 p.m. Use the official board for the sandwich — it does not print kaiser this pass.
verifiedStory: Eric and Cindy Hammersand opened Dry Dock on May 1, 1989, with about 100 seats and no restaurant experience; the Observer's 2015 sale story says they sold it that September to Gecko's Hospitality Group, and that the buyers kept the Dry Dock name, chefs, menu, and four boat slips. A 2022 Observer waterfront roundup instead says the restaurant "joined the Gecko's Hospitality Group in 1992." Both claims sit in the same paper; neither is resolved here. Official menu HTML this pass types Florida Grouper sandwich $30 as "locally caught" and does not print kaiser; Visit Sarasota's waterfront list still writes "The domestic grouper sandwich on a kaiser roll is the house specialty." Official Citrus Grouper $44 is "breaded & sautéed with our citrus cream sauce"; Observer 2022 names Florida orange juice and heavy cream reduced to nectar. Official Grouper Bites $25: crispy Florida Grouper with sweet chili sauce. Official pages now print hours (they did not on the 19 Aug pass).
funFact: Longboaters told the Hammersands they were crazy to open at the start of summer 1989. They later said that off-season opening is what let them learn before season hit.
currentUsefulDetail: Official hours: Sun–Thu 11am–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–9:30pm. To-go 11am–4pm, last pickup 4:30. Reservations: 941-383-0102 or online. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It is a Gecko's property, but it is not a Gecko's Grill & Pub — different name, different waterfront. Weekend waits are real; they take reservations.

name: PIER 22 Restaurant • Patio • Catering
vibeCheck: A Manatee River dining room and ballroom at the Bradenton Riverwalk — farmhouse lights on the Waterfront Terrace, the Green Bridge in the view.
whyGo: Pier 22 is the Miller family's Bradenton kitchen since 1976: local Gulf fish received whole and filleted by hand, and Grouper Artichoke Gratin still on the official menu. Chef Greg Campbell still directs this room — Grove in Lakewood Ranch is a different card.
bestFor: Date-night dinners, brunch, and anyone hosting on the river. It is a restaurant and an event house.
knownFor: Grouper artichoke gratin; Gulf fish received whole, filleted by hand
powerhouseProof: Official homepage copy: "50 YEARS WELCOMING YOU TO THE WATERFRONT." Official menu this pass: Grouper Artichoke Gratin $14; Grouper Sandwich on a house-made bun; Chef's Fresh Catch. Official event pages name the Waterside Terrace and Grand Ballroom. Official menu posts Sunday brunch 10 a.m.–3 p.m. and weekday lunch 11:30 a.m.–3 p.m. Monday–Saturday. Sarasota Magazine's waterfront list still cites grouper artichoke gratin and honey macadamia shrimp. SM listing hours: Monday–Thursday 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 11:30 a.m.–10:30 p.m.; Sunday 11 a.m.–10 p.m.
foodMove: Grouper artichoke gratin or honey macadamia shrimp — the dishes Sarasota Magazine still names. Campbell's kitchen cuts whole fish and steaks in-house.
drinkMove: Sit the Waterfront Terrace at dusk — the Green Bridge is the view.
insiderMove: Book the Waterside Terrace for the river and the Green Bridge; the Grand Ballroom is the wedding-scale room. Official brunch opens Sunday at 10 a.m.; the magazine listing instead opens Sunday at 11 a.m. Do not follow this pin to Grove on Main Street at Lakewood Ranch. Do not order honey macadamia shrimp off the 20 Aug official board — it is not listed.
verifiedStory: Official history places the restaurant on Memorial Pier: a municipal pier first built in 1878, later Corwin Dock, rebuilt and dedicated in 1930 to 21 Manatee County men who died in World War I. Official about this pass: family-owned and operated for decades on the Manatee River; from-scratch cuisine. Official about still says "go-to destination" — unused. Observer (July 2018) says Hugh Miller's family has owned Pier 22 since 1976, that the building is just under 30,000 square feet with its own ballroom, and that Greg Campbell had cooked for Miller for twelve years at that date. A February 2025 Observer piece still has Campbell directing both this kitchen and Grove, and says eight people at both rooms cut whole fish. Official menu JSON-LD this pass still lists Grouper Artichoke Gratin — "grouper, artichokes, three cheeses and pita bread" — $14. Official entrée copy: "Our local Gulf Coast fish are selected daily, received whole and filleted by hand in our refrigerated preparation room." Honey macadamia shrimp is not in official menu HTML this pass.
funFact: The official homepage sells limited-edition 50-year merchandise — they are marking a half-century on this dock.
currentUsefulDetail: Sarasota Magazine listing (hours go stale): Mon–Thu 11:30am–10pm; Fri–Sat 11:30am–10:30pm; Sun 11am–10pm. Phone 941-748-8087. Confirm on pier22.com. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: This is also a wedding and banquet house — Saturday evenings can feel like someone else's reception is in the next room.
