name: Skinny's Place
hours: Daily 11am–8pm (official site); island listing still says Tue–Sun
vibeCheck: A cash-only burger counter on Holmes Beach Gulf Drive, across from Manatee Public Beach — frosted mugs, onion rings, and the same family line since it was the Mid-Island Drive In in 1952.
whyGo: You come for a counter burger and a cold mug, not a dinner reservation. Skinny's has been the island's Mid-Island Drive In since 1952, still run by the original owners' grandchildren, a few steps from the public beach.
bestFor: A cheap, quick burger after the beach when you have cash. Skip it if you need cards, a full dinner menu, or a reserved table.
knownFor: Classic burgers, onion rings, and frosted beer mugs at a cash-only Holmes Beach counter that has been here since 1952.
powerhouseProof: Open since 1952 as the Mid-Island Drive In — the original owners' grandchildren still run it.
foodMove: A cheeseburger, hamburger, or bacon burger with onion rings — those are the plates the island listing actually names. No prices are posted online, so confirm at the counter. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: A frosted mug of beer, or wine if you want it — that is what the island listing puts on the bar.
insiderMove: Bring cash. The official site now posts daily 11am–8pm hours; the island listing still says Tuesday–Sunday, so confirm if you are aiming at a Monday.
verifiedStory: It opened in 1952 as the Mid-Island Drive In; the original owners' grandchildren still keep the counter going on Gulf Drive.
funFact: It sits directly across Gulf Drive from West Coast Surf Shop and across the street from Manatee Public Beach.
currentUsefulDetail: Official site: open every day 11am–8pm. The Anna Maria Island listing still says Tuesday–Sunday 11am–8pm and cash only. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: Cash only, and the online menu is a listing, not a live board — prices and Monday hours can disagree with the door.

name: The Ugly Grouper
vibeCheck: A big outdoor Holmes Beach seafood patio on Marina Drive — you eat under the 20-foot scrap-metal grouper, with live music every day and a kids play area off to the side.
whyGo: The Ugly Grouper is an Anna Maria Island outdoor seafood spot built on grouper: a sandwich of blackened, grilled, or fried filet on brioche with Cajun remoulade, and the Polynesian pineapple boat — blackened filet, garlic-parmesan risotto, and vegetables in a hollowed pineapple. The Reuben, cheese-fan tacos, and kabobs stay on the same fish.
bestFor: Families and groups who want outdoor seating, daily live music, and a kids play area with their seafood. Not the quiet-room dinner.
knownFor: The Ugly Grouper plates a grouper sandwich and Polynesian pineapple boat.
powerhouseProof: theuglygrouper.com/menu-1 prints Grouper Sandwich (brioche, Cajun remoulade) and Grouper Polynesian Boat (blackened filet, garlic-parmesan risotto, pineapple hull) plus Reuben, cheese-fan tacos, and kabobs. Official About prints statue size, weight, Rustic Steel Creations, and Dominique Martinez. annamariaisland.com independently names the cheese-fan grouper tacos.
foodMove: The grouper sandwich ($25) — blackened, grilled, or fried on a brioche bun with house Cajun remoulade. The Grouper Polynesian Boat ($36) is the bigger plate. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: The A.M.I. Sunset ($15) — frozen Cruzan silver rum with strawberry and mango — or the UG Perfect Margarita ($18) if you want a heavier pour.
insiderMove: Order the grouper sandwich or the Polynesian pineapple boat before you walk the statue. Cheese-fan tacos, the Reuben, and kabobs stay on the same fish. The metal grouper is wayfinding and a photo — keep it out of the first hook. Live music and frozen drinks (Coastal Colada, A.M.I. Sunset on the official drink list) are room notes, not the plate.
verifiedStory: The rail is the fish. The 20-foot scrap-metal grouper (official About: 3,180 lb, 20 × 14 × 10 feet, Rustic Steel Creations / Dominique Martinez, Tampa) is the island landmark and photo, not the first hook. The room is outdoor Holmes Beach seafood built around grouper sandwiches and the pineapple boat.
funFact: The yard statue weighs 3,180 pounds and measures 20 feet long, 14 feet tall, and 10 feet wide.
currentUsefulDetail: Open 7 days, 11am–10pm, lunch and dinner, with live music daily. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It is a loud outdoor patio with daily bands and a kids area — skip it if you want a quiet table. Several grouper plates sit in the mid-$20s to mid-$30s.

bestFor: Oyster and fried-seafood plates, weekend brunch, and groups who want a reservation-friendly seafood house. Skip it if you want a one-off independent shack — this is a multi-location Florida group.
knownFor: Gulf oysters, Rockefeller, and Chill towers — Casey Key raw bar
powerhouseProof: Official all-day menu this pass: Gulf oysters on the half shell (dozen $30 / half $16); Oysters Rockefeller $21 (creamy cheese, spinach, and bacon on the half shell); fried oysters $25; Little Chill $70; Big Chill $130 (whole Maine lobster, shrimp, half pound of snow crab, tuna tataki, a dozen oysters, chilled clams and mussels). Official locations page prints Casey Key hours as Sunday–Thursday 11 a.m.–9 p.m., Friday–Saturday 11 a.m.–10 p.m., brunch Saturday–Sunday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. Official homepage this pass also runs a Waterside "now open" line — unused, and not this pin.
foodMove: Start at the raw bar: Gulf oysters on the half shell (dozen $30) or Oysters Rockefeller ($21). The fried oyster plate ($25) or the oyster poboy ($26) if you want them cooked. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: The posted all-day menu pairs Oysters Rockefeller with a gin suggestion and the Big Chill tower with Champagne — confirm the current bar list; a separate beverage menu is on the site.
insiderMove: This pin is 482 Blackburn Point Road, Osprey — by the Casey Key swing bridge, not Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch. Observer 2022 describes the Big Chill with king crab; the official towers block now lists snow crab. The same official all-day page also prints a Little Chill with stone crab claws. Use the official tower you are ordering, not the 2022 write-up.
verifiedStory: Official locations list Casey Key at 482 Blackburn Point Road, Osprey, as its own room, separate from Waterside, Naples, Fort Myers, and Marco Island. A November 2022 Observer waterfront piece on this address describes Little Sarasota Bay views from the terrace or the dining room, a short throw from the historic swinging bridge to Casey Key, plus a raw bar and the Big/Little Chill towers, and names Phelan Family Brands. Official menu pages publish one brand all-day menu; they do not say this pin shares a kitchen with the other rooms. Official all-day menu this pass still types Gulf oysters on the half shell, Oysters Rockefeller, fried oysters, Little Chill, and Big Chill. The same official page lists Little Chill twice: dockside bites with "two medium stone crab claws"; seafood towers with "quarter pound of snow crab."

currentUsefulDetail: Casey Key location: Sun–Thu 11am–9pm, Fri–Sat 11am–10pm; brunch Sat–Sun 10am–2pm. Phone 941-770-3337. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: It is one store in a five-location Florida group, so the menu is shared, not a one-off. Several fish plates run market price, and the Big Chill tower is $130.

name: Dockside Waterfront Grill

vibeCheck: A tiki-covered waterfront grill at historic Fisherman's Wharf Marina on the Venice harbor — Marker 4 if you come by boat — with harbor and sunset views and a daily 3–6pm happy hour.
whyGo: Dockside Waterfront Grill plates fresh Gulf grouper — grilled, blackened, or fried — plus Fishcamp Chowder, the tomato-base pot made daily with clams and seafood. Official story dates Fisherman's Wharf to Captain Ben and Isa Mae Dunn in the 1950s; Gecko's owners Mike Gowan and Mike Quillen added the giant tiki.
bestFor: Sunset and boat-in dinners, dogs on the patio, and anyone who wants the harbor more than a sports-pub Gecko's. Skip it if you need a late kitchen — they close at 9pm.
knownFor: Gulf grouper, Fishcamp Chowder, and tiki chicken

name: Pelican Alley restaurant
hours: Hours not posted on the official site — call (941) 786-3616
vibeCheck: A rebuilt waterfront room on the Intracoastal at the south bridge to Casey Key — dock tables, seafood chowder, and Friday nights when Take 2 plays in the courtyard.
whyGo: Pelican Alley still prints The Alley's Famous Seafood Chowder — shrimp, scallops, clams, and fish under drawn butter — plus signature tapas such as seafood nachos and Scallops Soprano. Chadwick's Fish and Chips is tempura snapper, so the old fish-house names sit on the plate.
bestFor: Lunch or dinner on the Waterway, and Friday nights if you want live music in the courtyard. Skip it if you need posted hours or a transcribed online menu — both are missing.
knownFor: Pelican Alley seafood chowder, Chadwick's fish and chips, and signature tapas
powerhouseProof: Homepage copy names famous seafood chowder and signature tapas. The official menu images still list The Alley's Famous Seafood Chowder (cup/bowl), seafood nachos, Scallops Soprano, Crab Meat Fritters, and Chadwick's tempura snapper fish and chips.
foodMove: Start with the seafood chowder or the signature tapas they name on the homepage. The menu page is image-only and not transcribed, so confirm dishes and prices at the table. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: A specialty cocktail on the dock — that is the move they describe. They do not post a drink list as text.
insiderMove: Friday courtyard sets are Take 2; the official Take 2 page asks you to call ahead because those nights book up. Dock seating on the Waterway is homepage copy, not the hook. Keep address, hours, and phone off the rails.
verifiedStory: Official history still starts with the Chadwick fish house in the early 1900s, then the Sanders' Gulf-n-Bay, then the Arbuckles' Admiral's Wardroom. Robin Sweeney bought the room in 1981 and opened Pelican Alley after renovations. Hurricane Irma in 2017 forced a rebuild. Those names still land on the dinner board (Chadwick's Fish & Chips; The Admiral's Seafood Saute).
funFact: John D. MacDonald, who lived on Siesta Key, wrote a foreword to the Admiral's Wardroom cookbook when the Arbuckles ran the room.
currentUsefulDetail: Hours are not posted on the official site. Call 941-786-3616 for hours and reservations; they will not book by email. Friday courtyard: Take 2. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: No posted hours and no transcribed menu — you have to call. Ghost stories on the history page are their claim, not a verified fact for this card.

whyGo: Turtles plates a grouper sandwich — grilled, blackened, or fried with homemade tartar on brioche — plus mahi the same three ways and coconut-crusted mahi with pineapple rum sauce. Official copy dates the Little Sarasota Bay room to 1986 and six Siesta Key locals.
bestFor: Families, holiday meals, and anyone who wants a bay table without a fine-dining tab. Skip it if you want a late kitchen — they close at 9pm.
knownFor: Grouper sandwich, mahi sandwich, and coconut-crusted mahi

foodMove: The grouper sandwich ($22), grilled, blackened, or fried on brioche with house tartar. Turtle Pie ($10) if you want the namesake dessert. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: A Turtles Pain Killer or Turtles Deep Blue Sea ($10), or add a Bloody Mary or mimosa ($5.99) to Sunday brunch.
insiderMove: Keep the grouper and mahi; time Sunday brunch 10–1 only if that is the meal — the brunch clock is not the hook. Boat-in is Marker 48, or drive Midnight Pass on the south end of Siesta. name: The Lazy Lobster Of Longboat Key
hours: Summer: Mon–Sat 4–8:30pm, closed Sunday and closed for lunch
vibeCheck: A neighborhood lobster house on Gulf of Mexico Drive — Maine lobster, early-dining hour, and a garden terrace that only opens October through May.
whyGo: The Lazy Lobster of Longboat Key plates live Maine lobster supplied daily from Boothbay Harbor — the Maine lobster roll, Lazy Man out of the shell, and lobster mac. Michael Garey and Bob Fracalossy opened the room; Observer reporting says this is now the only Lazy Lobster left.
bestFor: Dinner with lobster as the point, early dining, and quieter summer weeknights. Skip it for lunch right now — summer hours cut midday service — and skip Sunday.
knownFor: Boothbay Harbor live lobster — roll, Lazy Man, and lobster mac
powerhouseProof: Official all-day lobster this pass: Maine lobster roll $39 (chilled, traditional dressing, grilled split-top roll); Lazy Man 5 oz $49 / 10 oz $89 (butter-poached, out of the shell); lobster mac dinner $49 (5 oz steamed Maine lobster, white cheese sauce, toasted crumbs, truffle oil). Official homepage text this pass lists seasonal summer hours as dinner only, Monday–Saturday 4–8:30 p.m., closed Sunday and closed for lunch; Early Dining 4–5:30 p.m.; Garden Terrace posted as seasonal, October through May. Official homepage also prints a summer locals deal — 15% off Early Dining or dinner Monday–Thursday, August 10 through September 30 — unused as a hook. Private dining is posted for 10–16 guests. Official address: 5350 Gulf of Mexico Drive, Longboat Key, FL 34228; (941) 383-0440.
foodMove: The Maine lobster roll ($39) or Lazy Man lobster (5 oz $49 / 10 oz $89) — butter-poached, out of the shell, no bib. Lobster mac and cheese dinner is $49. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: Happy hour house cocktails ($7.50) and house wines ($7) during the early window; the food-menu happy-hour block is not offered for to-go.
insiderMove: Official summer clock is dinner only; do not flatten that with the 2010 Observer listing that still showed daily lunch. Garden Terrace is posted October through May. Official about and the 2009 Observer use 5350; the 2010 Observer listing printed 5370 — leave that conflict in place. The 15% summer line is a dated deal, not the plate.
verifiedStory: Official about: Michael Garey (then a busser) and Bob Fracalossy (then the butcher) met at Café L'Europe on St. Armands Circle in 1979 and opened The Lazy Lobster of Longboat on October 15, 2009, in a Gulf of Mexico Drive space that had been hard on earlier restaurants. Observer (Oct. 21, 2024) retells that opening date and the unused terrace that sold Catherine Garey on the room. Observer (Nov. 24, 2009) places the opening at 5350 Gulf of Mexico Drive in the former Café on the Bay at Centre Shops; a March 2010 Observer listing printed 5370. Observer (May 25, 2022) says the Lockwood Ridge Lazy Lobster was converted to Kacey's, leaving Longboat as the only Lazy Lobster. House specialties on that menu include the Maine lobster roll, Lazy Man lobster, and lobster mac and cheese.
funFact: Entrée lobster is live Maine product from Boothbay Harbor; lobster tails and lobster tacos use Canadian cold-water tails instead.
currentUsefulDetail: Seasonal summer hours: closed for lunch; Monday–Saturday 4–8:30pm; closed Sunday. Posted through summer 2026. Monday–Thursday August 10–September 30: 15 percent off early dining until 5:30pm or the regular dinner menu 4–8:30pm. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: No lunch and no Sunday in this season, and lobster plates run from the high $30s into $80-plus. Book ahead if you want the 10–16-seat private room.
address: 5350 Gulf of Mexico Dr, Longboat Key

name: Myakka Outpost
vibeCheck: The park concession on Upper Myakka Lake — a gift shop, bike and canoe rentals, and (right now) a food truck next to the shop, not the repaired cafe building.
whyGo: You eat inside Myakka River State Park, after you pay the gate. The family has run the outpost since 1982; the plate they still name is homemade alligator stew, served now from a food truck while the main food building waits on repairs.
bestFor: A park-day lunch after a walk or paddle, when you already planned to pay admission. Skip it if you want a full dinner kitchen or you are not entering the park.
knownFor: The concession inside Myakka River State Park — homemade alligator stew, bike and canoe rentals, and a gift shop on Upper Myakka Lake, family-run since 1982.
powerhouseProof: Florida State Parks: locally owned and operated by the family since 1982, with bike and canoe rentals, a cafe, souvenirs, and camping supplies inside the park.
foodMove: Homemade alligator stew from the food truck — that is the plate both the official site and the state-park page still name. Seafood gumbo is the other park-page staple; confirm what the truck is actually serving that day. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: Beer and wine for guests 21 and over with ID, plus upstairs ice cream, drinks, and snacks in the gift shop.
insiderMove: Pay park admission at the gate first ($6 per vehicle for 2–8 people). The outpost is 9 miles east of I-75 exit 205, on the left. Rentals take no reservations and are subject to weather and water.
verifiedStory: The family has run Myakka Outpost inside the state park since 1982 as the concession — cafe, camp store, gifts, and rentals — on Upper Myakka Lake.
funFact: The official site currently serves food from a truck beside the gift shop because repairs on the main food-service building are delayed.
currentUsefulDetail: Food is coming from a food truck next to the gift shop while the main food-service building waits on repairs; alligator stew is still offered. Outpost hours 9am–5:30pm daily, closed Easter and Christmas. Park open 8am–sunset. Official site: Upper Myakka Lake and river water levels are at record lows and paddling is difficult. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: You have to enter the state park and pay admission. The cafe building is not the service point right now — it is a truck — and canoeing is a poor bet while the lake is that low.

name: Shore Longboat Key
vibeCheck: The Longboat Key Shore — a coastal seafood and cocktail room at 800 Broadway, south of Longboat Pass and west of Jewfish Key, with boat-in coordinates at ICW marker 39.

whyGo: Zio's Twelve 21 plates the Twelve21 Special — pepperoni, green peppers, onions, mushrooms, Italian sausage, and sliced meatballs — plus chicken piccata, lightly dusted and pan-seared in white-wine lemon butter with capers. Official about dates the Twelve 21 name to May 2018.
bestFor: A North Port pizza or Italian plate. Skip it Monday, and skip it if you need a posted dine-in close — official clocks are pickup and delivery.
knownFor: Twelve21 Special pizza and chicken piccata
powerhouseProof: Official location: 1221 S Sumter Blvd, North Port, FL 34287; (941) 426-9800. Posted pickup/delivery clocks: Monday Closed; Tue–Thu 3:30 p.m.–12:00 a.m.; Fri–Sat 4:00 p.m.–1:00 a.m.; Sun 7:00 p.m.–12:00 a.m. Official pages do not print a separate dine-in close.
foodMove: Cheese pizza is $14.95–$17.95. Chicken piccata is $21.95; veal marsala $23.95; chicken parm $21.95; penne a la vodka $17.95; fried calamari $14.95. (Live menu below.)
drinkMove: A priced bar list is not posted. Official pages are a pizzeria order board, not a cocktail room.
insiderMove: Skip Monday. Sunday pickup does not start until 7 p.m. Do not treat the midnight pickup clock as a posted dine-in close, and do not treat Visit Sarasota's lunch-trail line as the official board. The 40-year line is the owner's cooking story, not the restaurant's age. This is 1221 S. Sumter, North Port.
verifiedStory: Official about this pass: the room started as Zio's Pizza, then in May 2018 became Zio's Twelve 21 Pizzeria & Restaurant; the owner is a Cordon Bleu graduate (France) whose cooking started in his grandmother's Minnesota kitchen more than 40 years ago. Official pages do not print the owner's name. Footer: Pizzamico, LLC, 2026. Official menu HTML this pass types Twelve21 Special $17.95–$23.95 — "Pepperoni, green peppers, onions, mushrooms, Italian sausage & sliced meatballs"; Chicken Piccata $21.95 — "Lightly dusted & pan seared, finished in a white wine lemon butter sauce with capers"; Gnocchi Bolognese $18.95; Bianca Neve; Margherita. The same menu page headers "Currently offline" on the pickup-and-delivery widget this pass; dish HTML still loaded. Official homepage: sit-down or on the go; "known for our fresh ingredients" unused as our voice. Visit Sarasota (Discovering North Port itinerary) names fried calamari, stromboli, and toasted heroes and calls Zio's a lunch stop before the North Port Connector trail — official location clocks are afternoon/evening pickup and delivery.
funFact: The Twelve 21 name is the Sumter street number — 1221 — printed in the official rename line.
currentUsefulDetail: Pickup and delivery: Monday closed; Tuesday–Thursday 3:30pm–12am; Friday–Saturday 4pm–1am; Sunday 7pm–12am. Dine-in hours are not posted as text. Verified 2026-08-18; refresh before display.
watchOut: Do not treat the midnight pickup clock as a dine-in close. The 40-plus-years line is the owner’s cooking story, not the restaurant’s age.

name: Canopy Walk
hours: Park 8 a.m.–sunset daily. North Gate Sat, Sun, and state holidays 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
vibeCheck: A 100-foot suspension bridge hung in an oak-and-palm hammock, then a metal stair tower above the prairie. You hear the boards move under your feet.
whyGo: You walk a 100-foot treetop bridge 25 feet up, then 112 steps to a 74-foot tower — the first public canopy trail in North America, finished in 2000, inside Myakka River State Park.
bestFor: Hikers who want the hammock from above and can climb more than 100 stairs. Skip it if you need a Gulf beach or a stroller-only outing.
knownFor: A 100-foot walkway 25 feet up in an oak-and-palm hammock, plus a 74-foot tower on the William Boylston Nature Trail.
powerhouseProof: Florida State Parks calls this the first public treetop trail in North America. It opened in 2000 and sits in a 37,000-acre wild-and-scenic river park.
insiderMove: Take the short path a few hundred yards if you only want the walkway; the full Boylston loop is 0.8 mile. Pets stay on the trail, not on the structure — only leashed service dogs are allowed on the walkway.
verifiedStory: Canopy scientist Dr. Margaret D. Lowman of the TREE Foundation inspired the walkway. The Florida Park Service, Friends of Myakka River, and TREE Foundation built it; Friends and TREE still maintain it.
funFact: The tall tower is 112 steps. There is no extra fee beyond the park's $6-per-vehicle entry.
currentUsefulDetail: Drinking water has been temporarily unavailable since the park's 28 Oct 2025 notice; bottled water is free at the ranger station 8 a.m. to sunset. Refresh before display.
watchOut: More than 100 stairs. Park entry is $6 a vehicle. This pin is the walkway, not a Gulf swim.

name: Deer Prairie Creek Preserve
vibeCheck: Primitive dirt trail through flatwoods and dry prairie, with trailer parking at the Forbes Trail lot. You share the path with horses, not beach wagons.
whyGo: A 7,335-acre preserve that protects Deer Prairie Creek and nearly six miles of the Myakka River's east bank, with more than 60 miles of primitive trail.
bestFor: Hikers, riders, and birders who want a full-day wild walk. Skip it if you want pavement, restrooms beyond a picnic shelter, or a short stroller loop.
knownFor: Co-managed Myakka-creek country — scrub-jay habitat, a two-pole picnic shelter, and a North Port Connector trailhead onto the Legacy Trail.
powerhouseProof: Sarasota County and SWFWMD co-own 7,335 acres here. The north lot is the Atlas pin: 7001 Forbes Trail, Venice.
insiderMove: Start at the north entrance on Forbes Trail. Download the county brochure and map before you lose signal. Dogs, if you bring one, stay leashed.
verifiedStory: The preserve is named for Deer Prairie Creek, a tributary of the state-designated Wild and Scenic Myakka. There is no fence between this land and the south side of SWFWMD's Schewe Ranch.
funFact: The north lot has a small two-pole shelter with one picnic table — that is the shade, not a restroom building.
currentUsefulDetail: County notice dated 4 Aug 2026: north and south temporarily closed for USDA aerial feral-hog work. Confirm the gate is open before you drive. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Primitive natural-surface trail. This card is the Forbes Trail / north entrance, not the Tamiami south gate.

name: Maxine Barritt Park
vibeCheck: A picnic pavilion and a paved loop around a fenced lake, then a boardwalk to Gulf sand between the dog beach and the fishing pier.
whyGo: The picnic park between Brohard Paw Park and the Venice Fishing Pier — a wheelchair-accessible boardwalk to the Gulf, a lake loop, and restrooms the county lists on site.
bestFor: A family picnic that ends on Venice sand. Skip it if you want a lifeguard tower or a dog on the beach — Brohard next door is the dog sand; Venice Beach is the guarded lot.
knownFor: A passive Gulf picnic park with grills, a tot lot, and a paved trail around a manmade lake. City-owned, county-maintained.
powerhouseProof: Brohard, next door, is the only county dog beach. The pier is the other neighbor. This one is the 2010 passive picnic park between them.
insiderMove: Dogs stay on a leash no longer than six feet in the parking and on the paths. They are not allowed on the sand or the beach boardwalk.
verifiedStory: Maxine Barritt, a community activist, lobbied to keep this a passive park when it was built around 2010. The city still names her. The land is inside Venice; the county maintains it.
funFact: Visit Venice points you around the fenced lake for birds — and says you may see an alligator.
currentUsefulDetail: No Healthy Beaches station is named Maxine Barritt; the nearest listed neighbor is BROHARD PARK. Refresh before display.
watchOut: No lifeguard on this stretch. County lists swimming; the guarded tower is Venice Beach.

name: Neal Preserve
vibeCheck: A short shell-and-boardwalk walk through mangrove and oak hammock, with a 20-foot tower and reconstructed mounds just south of the Anna Maria bridge.
whyGo: A 120-acre coastal walk off the Anna Maria bridge — mangrove, salt tern, oak hammock, a 20-foot tower, and reconstructed burial mounds the county calls an open-air museum.
bestFor: A quiet hour of boardwalk and history before or after the island. Skip it if you want a Gulf swim, a dog walk, or a long trail.
knownFor: A half-mile of shell and boardwalk past reconstructed mounds. The Smithsonian excavated the originals in the 1930s; the county dates habitation here from 3000 BC to 1400 AD.
powerhouseProof: Perico, east along Manatee Avenue, is the bird-sanctuary conversion. This pin is the mound-and-tower preserve on the south side of the bridge.
insiderMove: Overflow parking is north of the bridge. One portable restroom sits in the lot. Leave bikes on the racks; they are not allowed on the trails.
verifiedStory: The county asks you to treat the reconstructed mounds as protected ground. Collecting is not allowed.
funFact: The shell-trail loop the county lists is 0.3 mile; the full shell-and-boardwalk walk is about half a mile.
currentUsefulDetail: Open sunrise to sunset every day. Official pages do not print an admission fee. Refresh before display.
watchOut: No pets. This is not a swim beach. The county lists fishing access; there is no lifeguard.

name: Perico Preserve
vibeCheck: A half-mile trail through restored wetland and planned scrub, with a bird blind and an observation dock. Quiet on purpose — dogs stay home.
whyGo: The county built this as a bird sanctuary on former farmland — a bird blind, an observation dock, and a half-mile trail. Dogs stay home except service dogs.
bestFor: Birders and a short wetland walk. Skip it if you want to bring a dog or need a long paved loop — Robinson is the bigger neighbor.
knownFor: Restored coastal wetlands and planned scrub hills on Perico Island, with bikes limited to designated trails.
powerhouseProof: The county's own page calls it the first preserve here fully conceptualized as a bird sanctuary. Neal, west along the same road, is the mound-and-tower pin.
insiderMove: At marked points you leave the bike and walk. The covered pavilion at the west lot has three picnic benches.
verifiedStory: The land was farmland when the county acquired it. The official page describes the conversion to coastal wetland, scrub hills, and upland.
funFact: The county asks you to watch from the bird blind — sit, use binoculars, or rest a camera on an opening — instead of walking up on the birds.
currentUsefulDetail: Open sunrise to sunset every day. Official pages do not print acreage or an admission fee. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Not a swim beach. Official page does not print a trail mileage beyond the half-mile walk and does not print a restroom building.

name: Shamrock Park Nature Center
hours: Park 6 a.m. to sunset. Nature Center Saturdays 9 a.m.–1 p.m.
vibeCheck: Coastal scrub and a paved Intracoastal path that dumps you onto the Venetian Waterway and the Legacy Trail, with a small nature center that opens Saturday morning.
whyGo: Venice's Intracoastal trailhead — a paved multi-use path that ties into Venetian Waterway Park and the Legacy Trail, plus a nature center that opens Saturday 9 to 1.
bestFor: Walkers, cyclists, and anyone who wants coastal scrub that still holds Florida scrub-jays. Skip it if you need a Gulf swim — Caspersen is across the water.
knownFor: Coastal scrub with Florida scrub-jays and gopher tortoises, plus basketball, tennis, a playground, and a Florida-friendly demonstration garden.
powerhouseProof: Visit Sarasota calls this some of the last remaining scrub habitat on the county's coast. The county lists a 2.3-mile paved trail on the Intracoastal.
insiderMove: Drop into the nature center Saturday 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. for fossil, shell, and artifact displays. The plant clinic is the second Saturday — no signup.
funFact: The county trail figure is 2.3 miles paved; Visit Sarasota lists 1.2 miles through the central park. Follow the trail map, not the smaller number.
currentUsefulDetail: County lists leash-required dogs; Visit Sarasota says pets are prohibited. Follow the posted sign. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Do not assume a dog is welcome. Confirm the sign at the gate. This is not Caspersen Beach.

name: The Bishop Museum of Science and Nature
hours: Tue–Sat 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sun noon–5 p.m.; closed Monday
vibeCheck: A downtown Bradenton museum with a 50-foot planetarium, a working manatee rehab tank, and an indoor backyard for kids — closed Mondays.
whyGo: You get a 50-foot full-dome planetarium, the Parker Manatee Rehabilitation Habitat, and the Mosaic Backyard Universe in one downtown ticket, a short walk from the Riverwalk.
bestFor: Families and anyone who wants a planetarium show plus a live rehab manatee. Skip it on Monday, and skip it if you only have time for a beach.
knownFor: Gulf Coast natural history from the Pleistocene to now, a 50-foot planetarium, and more than 40 rehab manatees hosted since 1998.
powerhouseProof: The museum's own about page calls it the largest natural history museum on Florida's Gulf Coast. The Parker habitat has been part of the Manatee Rescue and Rehabilitation Partnership since 1998.
foodMove: Eat outside. Food and drinks stay out of the galleries; water is allowed. Picnic tables sit in front of the main door, and Main Street is a short walk.
insiderMove: Buy the ticket before you arrive. Planetarium doors lock at showtime; late entry is not allowed. Free street parking on 10th Street West is three hours.
verifiedStory: The Parker Manatee Rehabilitation Habitat is part of Florida's Manatee Rescue and Rehabilitation Partnership and has housed more than 40 rehabilitating manatees since 1998.
funFact: The official about page names the Montague Tallant collection of prehistoric and early post-contact artifacts among the highlights.
currentUsefulDetail: Adult ticket $25. Official home and plan-your-visit pages disagree on some closed holidays (New Year's Eve, Labor Day, Christmas Eve, Easter). Call 941-746-4131 before a holiday visit. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Closed Monday. Food stays outside except water. Doors lock when a planetarium show starts.

name: Palma Sola Botanical Park
hours: 8 a.m. to dusk daily; confirm the calendar — weddings can close the grounds
vibeCheck: Ten quiet acres of palms and rare fruit trees on a former county nursery in Old Palma Sola. Donation boxes, not a gate fee.
whyGo: A free 10-acre former county nursery — rare fruit trees, palms, and a frost-free pocket of northwest Bradenton, open 8 a.m. to dusk unless a wedding takes the grounds.
bestFor: A slow walk among named fruit trees. Skip it if you need a beach, and call first on a weekend — they close for weddings.
knownFor: The 2008 Manatee Rare Fruit Council planting: star fruit, dragon fruit, jackfruit, lychee, sapodilla, tamarind, and more, with no gate fee.
powerhouseProof: Official copy calls this Manatee County's only botanical gardens and says it stays free 365 days on donations — no local, state, or federal subsidy.
insiderMove: Check the park calendar before you go. The Hidden Garden Nursery is Tuesday and Saturday 9 a.m. to noon, October through May.
verifiedStory: Neighbors rallied in 1990 to save the 10-acre Manatee County Nursery as surplus land. The Palma Sola Botanical Park Foundation incorporated as a 501(c)(3) in 1993. The Galleria went in after 2000; the Baden office was a florist shop moved onto the property.
funFact: The official visit page lists the 2008 fruit section by name — star fruit, dragon fruit, jackfruit, lychee, sapodilla, noni, ylang ylang — on a frost-free 10 acres.
currentUsefulDetail: Free, 8 a.m. to dusk, but weekend weddings close the park. Groups of 10 or more: call 941-761-2866; suggested donation $10 a person. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Do not assume a Saturday is open. This is not Selby, and it is not Palma Sola Causeway.

name: Payne Park
hours: Restrooms 8 a.m.–10 p.m. Skate park daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m. Tennis hours vary; reservations required.
vibeCheck: A downtown rec park on the old spring-training grounds — circus playground, unsupervised skate bowl, disc golf, and twelve Har-Tru courts.
whyGo: The downtown Sarasota park that used to be spring training — now a circus playground, a free skate park, disc golf, and twelve Har-Tru tennis courts.
bestFor: Families using Circus Park, skaters, and tennis players. Skip it if you want a quiet preserve or a Gulf beach.
knownFor: Payne Park from 1924 to 1989 as the spring home of the New York Giants, Boston Red Sox, and Chicago White Sox, on 60 acres Calvin and Martha Payne donated.
powerhouseProof: The stadium closed in 1989 when Ed Smith Stadium replaced it. The same grounds now hold Circus Park, a free skate park, and a Legacy Trail connector.
foodMove: The city lists food and beverage on site — the park café. Confirm it is open; the official page does not print a café clock.
insiderMove: Circus Park is the splash-and-slide playground — pets stay out unless they are service animals. Tennis needs a reservation.
verifiedStory: Calvin Payne and his wife, Martha, donated 60 acres. The professional ballpark stood here from 1924 to 1989.
funFact: The city still names the New York Giants, Boston Red Sox, and Chicago White Sox as the spring clubs that used this field.
currentUsefulDetail: Atlas pin is 2050 Adams Ln; the city lists 2010 Adams Ln. Skate park is free, daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m., unsupervised. Refresh before display.
watchOut: No single park-wide clock on the official page — restrooms, skate, and tennis run on different hours. The skate park is at your own risk.

name: Jiggs Landing
hours: Preserve sunrise to sunset, 365 days. Night ramp access by $30 gate card from G.T. Bray.
vibeCheck: A small freshwater landing on Evers Reservoir — replica cabin, kayak beach, fishing pier, and a bait shop whose clock is not the park clock.
whyGo: A freshwater fish-camp landing on Evers Reservoir — county preserve, a replica cabin, a kayak launch, and a boat ramp you can unlock before sunrise with a $30 gate card.
bestFor: Paddlers and freshwater anglers. Skip it if you want Gulf surf or a saltwater ramp.
knownFor: Al (Jiggs) and Agnes Metcalf's 1944 camp on the Braden River, bought by the county in 2005 as a 4.5-acre launch.
powerhouseProof: County paddle notes: boat launch, picnic shelters, fishing pier, restrooms, and a handicap-accessible kayak launch, plus a replica of an original cabin.
foodMove: Concession and bait are the Jiggs Landing Outpost, not the county. Call 941-727-4181. Do not treat those hours as the preserve clock.
insiderMove: The preserve is sunrise to sunset. Night ramp access is a one-time $30 card sold at G.T. Bray Recreation Center; a replacement is $5.
verifiedStory: The Metcalfs bought seven acres in 1944 and ran a fish camp on the Braden River for more than 40 years. Manatee County acquired the 4.5-acre landing from the City of Bradenton and the former owners in 2005.
funFact: You launch from a small beach, a ramp, or a stationary dock into the Braden River and Evers Reservoir — freshwater license south of the dam for ages 16 and up.
currentUsefulDetail: Preserve sunrise to sunset. Outpost bait, cabin, and rental hours are separate. Refresh before display.
watchOut: This is not Braden River Park. Freshwater rules apply on this side of the dam. Outpost Facebook is not a source for this card.

name: Fort Hamer Park
hours: Sunrise to sunset, unless posted or permitted.
vibeCheck: A small riverside lot under the Fort Hamer Bridge — trailers, a kayak dock, and a youth-rowing boathouse. You came to put a boat on the Manatee, not to find Gulf sand.
whyGo: A 7.3-acre Manatee River launch next to the Fort Hamer Bridge — boat ramp, kayak dock, fishing pier, and the county youth-rowing boathouse.
bestFor: Paddlers and boaters heading onto the Upper Manatee. Skip it if you want a playground campus or Gulf sand.
knownFor: The public ramp on the Upper Manatee River State Canoe Trail, plus two reservable pavilions beside the rowing facility.
powerhouseProof: County lists 7.3 acres here. Paddle Manatee puts this ramp on the five-mile Upper Manatee River State Canoe Trail, a Florida Greenways and Trails designation.
insiderMove: East of the ramp is the slow, shaded canoe water. West opens to boat traffic — take a sea kayak that way.
verifiedStory: Fort Hamer was built in 1849 on the south shore across from today's ramp, named for a Florida Volunteers brigadier general. A garrison of 165 stood down in 1850; the site saw brief service again in the Third Seminole War, 1855 to 1858.
funFact: The historic fort stood across the river from the public ramp you use now.
currentUsefulDetail: Sunrise to sunset. No overnight parking (Ordinance 23-121). Pavilion 1 is $60 plus tax with electric; pavilion 2 is $50 plus tax, no electric. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Water spigots are not for public use. This is not Jiggs Landing and not Ray's Canoe Hideaway.

name: Red Bug Slough
vibeCheck: Oak shade and a dirt path a few blocks off Beneva, with a swing set at the lot and a pier on the slough. Suburban preserve, not Celery Fields and not a Gulf beach.
whyGo: A 72-acre suburban preserve on Beneva — hammock, pine flatwoods, seasonal wetlands, and the slough itself, with a fishing pier and a small playground by the lot.
bestFor: A short bird walk or a leashed dog on county rules. Skip it if you want a long primitive day — Deer Prairie is the big one.
knownFor: The slough older residents called Skeeter Drain, bought in 2001 through the county Environmentally Sensitive Lands Protection Program and Florida Forever.
powerhouseProof: The county kiosk names 72 acres, two picnic shelters, and a fishing pier on the slough. The facility page lists paved and unpaved trail, restrooms, and leash-required dogs.
insiderMove: Download the county map before you go. The Beneva lot is the signed parking; Visit Sarasota also lists walk-through gates.
verifiedStory: Residents called this Skeeter Drain because the water runs through the site into Phillippi Creek, about a mile and a half northwest. Partial amenity funding came from the Nature Conservancy's Natural Heritage Fund for Sarasota County.
funFact: The name is literal — the kiosk tells you to look for a scarlet skimmer dragonfly or a red cotton stainer beetle.
currentUsefulDetail: Open 6 a.m. to sunset. County lists leash-required dogs. Visit Sarasota says parking is limited. Refresh before display.
watchOut: This is not Celery Fields. Follow the posted dog rule; the county page requires a leash.

name: Florida Railroad Museum
hours: Ticket office Wednesday–Sunday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Train rides weekends only.
vibeCheck: A rural Parrish rail yard — open-air coaches, air-conditioned cars, and a gift shop that opens on weekdays when the locomotives stay parked.
whyGo: The Florida Railroad Museum runs the Willow Express from Parrish to Willow on historic diesel cars, not the Venice Train Depot. Official ride copy calls it a 13-mile, hour-and-a-half trip, rain or shine, with a layover at the replica Seaboard Air Line station. Volunteer crews operate the six-mile early-1900s SAL line in rural Manatee County.
bestFor: Families who want a weekend train ride. Skip it on a weekday if you came to see the engines; those stay closed.
knownFor: Parrish–Willow Willow Express on historic diesel cars
powerhouseProof: 12210 83rd Street East, Parrish, FL 34219; 941-776-0906. About/contact: ticket office / gift shop / model railroad Wednesday–Sunday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Rides weekends only; Willow Express 13 miles / ~1.5 hours, rain or shine. Annual pass from $45. Wheelchair: ramp into one open-air coach, no restroom, no between-car access. Official pages fetched this pass do not print a standing Willow Express fare.
insiderMove: This is 12210 83rd Street East in Parrish — not the Venice Train Depot. If you came to see locomotives, come on a weekend; weekday admission is the shop and the model railroad. Call 941-776-0906 before you drive. Do not quote an 11 a.m. / 2 p.m. pair as official — that clock is Wikipedia / county-pass copy, not the ride page. Do not invent a fare.
verifiedStory: Official home/about this pass: founded as The Florida Gulf Coast Railroad Museum to preserve Florida railroad history; six-mile SAL line, early 1900s, abandoned 1986 after the 1967 ACL/SAL merger; volunteer crews; replica SAL station at Willow; diesel-powered excursions on open-air, open-window, and air-conditioned cars. Homepage Willow Express blurb this pass: “1.5 hour round-trip excursion to Willow, FL on our historic railroad equipment.” Official pages fetched this pass do not print a founding year. Wikipedia: 1981 founding, 1984 state-museum statute, weekend excursions since 1992.
funFact: Wheelchair boarding is a ramp into one open-air coach; that car has no restroom, and you cannot roll between cars.
currentUsefulDetail: Weekend rides only; check the calendar. Ticket office 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday. Weekday admission to the shop and model railroad is free. Official pages do not print a standing Willow Express fare. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Historic cars are not wheelchair-accessible between cars. This is not the Venice Train Depot.

name: Sarasota Art Museum
hours: Galleries Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. Closed Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's Day.
vibeCheck: Collegiate neo-Gothic brick on Tamiami, then white galleries and a plaza lawn — a high school that now hangs temporary shows.
whyGo: A contemporary kunsthalle — no permanent collection — in the 1926 M. Leo Elliott Sarasota High School, with 15,000 square feet of galleries across three floors.
bestFor: Anyone who wants current art, not a standing collection. Skip it if you came for Ringling's Old Masters — that campus is north.
knownFor: Rotating 20th- and 21st-century shows on the Ringling College Museum Campus, plus the 1957 Paul Rudolph support building and a 1959 Victor Lundy store.
powerhouseProof: Official copy calls it the region's first museum dedicated to contemporary art and a kunsthalle. Adult ticket $20; 17 and under free.
foodMove: Bistro is in the Paul Rudolph building — sandwiches, soup, coffee, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily. Outside food is not allowed on campus.
insiderMove: Free Second Sundays. Park in the first six rows on the south lot; rows seven and beyond are reserved for Sarasota High School Monday through Friday until 2 p.m.
verifiedStory: In 2003, 13 Sarasotans started the museum idea. After two years of talks they partnered with Ringling College to turn the historic high school into galleries and classrooms.
funFact: The campus also keeps five acres of outdoor ground for sculpture and events, including the Marcy and Michael Klein Plaza.
currentUsefulDetail: Tickets sell until 4:30 p.m. the same day. Food stays out of the galleries. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Closed six holidays. Pets stay home except service animals. This is not The Ringling.

name: Florida Studio Theatre
hours: Box office Monday 9 a.m.–6 p.m.; Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–9 p.m.; Sunday 11 a.m.–9 p.m.
vibeCheck: A tight downtown campus around Palm and Cocoanut — the old Woman's Club at the Atlas pin, plus cabaret rooms and a lab you walk between.
whyGo: Five small downtown theatres on two blocks — Mainstage, cabaret, Stage III, children's shows, and improv — from a company that started by touring prisons and migrant camps.
bestFor: A play or cabaret night downtown. Skip it if you want a 1,000-seat opera house — that is Pineapple Avenue.
knownFor: Official copy calls it the largest subscription theatre in Florida, with more than 38,000 subscribers and more than 20 professional productions a year.
powerhouseProof: Founded in 1973 by Jon Spelman. Richard Hopkins took over in 1980 with about 100 subscribers. Five stages now sit across three buildings.
foodMove: Green Room Cafe and the cabaret restaurants. Official menu names lobster bisque, coconut shrimp, and tortellini Alfredo. Food bought on site can go into the theatres.
insiderMove: Park in the Palm Avenue garage; the first two hours are free. Arrive 30 minutes early. Cabaret and improv dining opens an hour before curtain.
verifiedStory: Local backers put FST in the Historic Women's Club in 1977 as a 72-seat house. They finished paying for it in 1985 and renamed it the Keating Theatre in 2003 for Ed and Elaine Keating.
funFact: The Atlas pin is the Keating at 1241 N. Palm. Goldstein Cabaret is 1239 N. Palm; Gompertz, Court Cabaret, and Bowne's Lab sit at 1265 First Street.
currentUsefulDetail: $2 fee on each single ticket. Exchanges until 48 hours before curtain; $5 for non-subscribers. Tickets are final sale. Official history still says 49th season — founded 1973, so treat the season count as stale and use the year. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Late seating is not guaranteed. No recording during the show. This is not Asolo and not Van Wezel.

name: Sarasota Opera House
vibeCheck: Cream stucco and a three-story atrium on Pineapple — a downtown show night, not a daytime walk-through.
whyGo: A 1,119-seat house that opened 10 April 1926 as the A.B. Edwards Theater — Mediterranean Revival on Pineapple, still producing opera in the room the first mayor built.
bestFor: Opera season and anyone who wants the 1926 room. Skip it if you want a casual cabaret — that is Florida Studio Theatre.
knownFor: The winter opera festival in a company-owned 1926 theatre, plus symphony, ballet, film, and comedy in the same hall.
powerhouseProof: Official seating is 1,119 in the William E. Schmidt Opera Theatre. The company bought the building in 1979 for $173,000 and calls itself the seventh U.S. opera company to own its house.
insiderMove: Box office is weekday 10 to 4. 2026 is the building's centennial year; confirm what is on the calendar before you go.
verifiedStory: A.B. Edwards, Sarasota's first mayor, hired Jacksonville architect Roy A. Benjamin. Opening night had eight shops, twelve offices, and twelve apartments around a central atrium. Will Rogers played 1927; Elvis played 1956; The Greatest Show on Earth had its road premiere here on 31 January 1952.
funFact: A 1928 hurricane wrecked the Robert Morton pipe organ. The 2007–2008 gut renovation cost $20 million and dug a larger orchestra pit.
currentUsefulDetail: Official home page lists the company's 68th season and weekday box-office hours. Single tickets were online-only at last check, with phone and in-person sales listed from 1 September. Refresh before display.
watchOut: This is a show night, not a museum. Van Wezel is the purple bayfront hall; this is the 1926 house on Pineapple.

name: G.T. Bray Park
hours: Park sunrise to sunset. Recreation Center Monday–Thursday 5:30 a.m.–9 p.m.; Friday 5:30 a.m.–7 p.m.; Saturday–Sunday 7 a.m.–4 p.m.
vibeCheck: Ball fields, a pool complex, and a rec-center parking lot in west Bradenton — a working county campus, not a preserve.
whyGo: Manatee County's 140-acre rec campus — fields, an aquatic center with lifeguards, a skate park, disc golf, a dog park, and a rec center you enter on a daily fee or a membership.
bestFor: Families, league sports, and a weekday workout. Skip it if you want a quiet boardwalk or Gulf sand.
knownFor: The county membership desk ($25 / $35 / $90 a month plus tax) plus an almost 1.5-mile asphalt trail that ties this campus to 51st Street Park.
powerhouseProof: County amenities list the rec center, aquatic center, skate park, tennis, pickleball, splash pad, and an 18-hole disc golf course at 51st Street Park.
insiderMove: The skate park is sunrise to sunset, at your own risk, and closes when the equipment is wet. The teen room is unsupervised; non-members pay $3 to drop in.
verifiedStory: The rec center is the paid core — fitness, basketball, and (on higher memberships) group exercise, pickleball, and clay tennis. The grounds stay sunrise to sunset without that card.
funFact: The fitness trail is the connector: a shaded asphalt path with exercise stations between G.T. Bray and 51st Street Park.
currentUsefulDetail: Recreation membership $25 a month plus tax; Recreation Plus $35; tennis $90 at this location only. SilverSneakers and Renew Active accepted. Pool hours are not printed on the park page — call 941-742-5923. Refresh before display.
watchOut: Do not treat rec-center hours as park hours. This is not Payne Park and not John Marble.

name: Centennial Park

vibeCheck: A landscaped downtown square ringed by shops — picnic tables, a kiosk, and kids in the fountain, not a Gulf beach.

funFact: The fountain is kept to swimming-pool standards by Public Works.

watchOut: This is not Brohard and not Maxine Barritt. No lifeguard on the fountain.

name: Venice Performing Arts Center

funFact: Each of the three resident companies presents three to seven performances in the winter season.

name: Ray's Canoe Hideaway

vibeCheck: A river-bank outfitter at the end of Hagle Park Road — boats, a small store, and no lifeguard.
whyGo: A private fee launch onto the Upper Manatee River State Canoe Trail — rent a canoe or kayak, or put your own boat in, then paddle toward Rye Preserve or the dam.
bestFor: A half-day paddle on the shaded upper river. Skip it if you want a free county ramp — Fort Hamer is that.
knownFor: The county paddle guide's named private launch on the five-mile Greenways-and-Trails canoe water east of Fort Hamer.
powerhouseProof: Official hours page: canoe $25 half day / $30 full day for two people; own-boat launch $6, or $9 with overnight parking. Cash, local checks, travelers checks — no cards.

watchOut: No credit cards on the printed page. This is not Fort Hamer and not Jiggs Landing.

name: Bobby Jones Golf Club
hours: Nature park dawn to dusk; closed when the golf course is closed. Golf by tee time.
vibeCheck: A restored municipal Donald Ross course beside a free wetland trail. Carts and walkers share Circus Boulevard with people who only came to walk the old cart paths.
whyGo: You play the 1926 Ross eighteen the city restored, or you skip the fee and walk the Marlon Brown Eagle Trail around the new wetlands — same Circus Boulevard property either way.
bestFor: A municipal round or a free dawn walk. Skip it if you want a Gulf beach or a private club.
knownFor: A 1926 Donald Ross municipal eighteen, renamed in 1927 for Robert Tyre Jones Jr., plus a free nature trail off the driving range.
powerhouseProof: City parks: the Ross course opened to the public in 1926. A 2023 city release calls the 307-acre property the city's largest green space and records a 2022 conservation easement.

watchOut: The nature park closes when the golf course is closed. This is not Payne Park and not Celery Fields.

name: Sarasota Sailing Squadron
hours: Grounds Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–7 p.m. Lessons by appointment.
vibeCheck: A working community sail yard on City Island — hoists, dinghy racks, and a clubhouse that started as eight poles and a roof. You came to get a boat on the bay, not to sit in a private dining room.
whyGo: A 501(c)(3) community sailing club that takes non-members for two-hour lessons on Hobie Waves, Getaways, and American 18s — the same City Island shore as Mote and the Ski-A-Rees.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to learn to sail or paddle from City Island. Skip it if you only want a yacht-club dinner.
knownFor: Public learn-to-sail on Sarasota Bay, plus racks for Sunfish, Lasers, kayaks, and stand-up boards.
powerhouseProof: Official governance: a 501(c)(3) nonprofit open to anyone interested in sailing and other non-motorized water sports. Official about: more than 70 years on the bay.
foodMove: The clubhouse and patio serve drinks and snacks after a sail. Old Salty Dog is next door at 1601 Ken Thompson Parkway.
insiderMove: Park outside the Squadron grounds. Weekday hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Call 941-388-2355 to book a lesson.
verifiedStory: Teenagers started a club on the City Pier — now Marina Jack — in the late 1930s. It shut down in 1942, then came back after the war as the Sarasota Sailing Squadron and moved to City Island in 1958 when the pier came down. Ralph Twitchell designed the first clubhouse; Tim Seibert designed the Stone House.
funFact: The first clubhouse was eight power poles holding up a roof.
currentUsefulDetail: Non-member lesson $225 a person for two hours; a friend is $80 more. Members pay $100 / $60. Confirm before you book. Refresh before display.
watchOut: This is a volunteer club with a weekday grounds clock, not a drop-in marina. There is no fuel on site — only free water at the end of the main dock.

name: Sarasota Ski-A-Rees
hours: Free Sunday shows at 2 p.m. in season. Confirm the current calendar.
vibeCheck: A small City Island lot past Mote — bleachers, a dock, and ski boats on the bay. You came for a free Sunday show, not a ticketed theatre.

bestFor: A Sunday afternoon on City Island. Skip it in the mid-season gap, or if you need a guaranteed indoor show.
knownFor: Free Sunday 2 p.m. water-ski shows on Ken Thompson Park, and a 2017 national show-ski title.
powerhouseProof: Official: a Sarasota tradition since 1957 and a 501(c)(3). About 80 active members, ages 3 to over 70. 2017 National Show Ski Tournament champions — the team's first national title.
foodMove: The team sells drinks, candy, and T-shirts at shows. Old Salty Dog is next door on Ken Thompson Parkway.
insiderMove: Turn through the Mote Marine lot and continue to the end; the Ski-A-Rees lot is the last right. The phone is monitored on weekends.
verifiedStory: The amateur team has staged themed shows on this site since 1957. Membership is open with board approval; visitors are asked to come most Saturday or Sunday and introduce themselves.
funFact: The 2017 national-title show was Star Wars: The Skiquel.

watchOut: There is no daily gate. Midsummer can be a gap between seasons. The phone — 941-388-1666 — is watched on weekends only.

name: The Fish Hole

name: Duffy's Tavern
